Ko e kamataʻanga ʻoe ongoongolelei ʻa Sisu Kalaisi, ko e ʻAlo ʻoe ʻOtua;
The beginning of the gospel of Jesus Christ, the Son of God;
‌ʻO hangē ko ia ʻoku tohi ʻi he kau palōfita, “Vakai, ʻoku ou fekau atu hoku fakamelomelo ke muʻomuʻa ʻi ho ʻao, ʻaia te ne teuteu ho hala kiate koe.
As it is written in the prophets, Behold, I send my messenger before thy face, which shall prepare thy way before thee.
Ko e leʻo ʻoe tokotaha ʻoku kalanga ʻi he toafa, ‘Mou teuteu ʻae hala ʻoe ʻEiki, fakatonutonu hono ngaahi ʻaluʻanga.’”
The voice of one crying in the wilderness, Prepare ye the way of the Lord, make his paths straight.
Naʻe papitaiso ʻe Sione ʻi he toafa, mo ne malangaʻaki ʻae papitaiso ʻoe fakatomala ki he fakamolemole ʻoe angahala.
John did baptize in the wilderness, and preach the baptism of repentance for the remission of sins.
Pea naʻe ʻalu atu kiate ia ʻae fonua kotoa pē ko Siutea, pea mo kinautolu ʻo Selūsalema, ʻonau papitaiso kotoa pē ʻiate ia ʻi he vaitafe ko Sioatani, ʻo vete ʻenau ngaahi angahala.
And there went out unto him all the land of Judaea, and they of Jerusalem, and were all baptized of him in the river of Jordan, confessing their sins.
Pea naʻe kofuʻaki ʻa Sione ʻae fulufuluʻi kāmeli, pea nonoʻo ʻaki hono konga loto ʻae kiliʻi manu; pea naʻa ne kai ʻae heʻe mo e meʻa huʻamelie ʻoe vao;
And John was clothed with camel’s hair, and with a girdle of a skin about his loins; and he did eat locusts and wild honey;
Pea naʻa ne malanga, ʻo pehē, “ʻOku muimui ʻiate au ʻae tokotaha ʻoku lahi kiate au, ko e nonoʻo ʻoe topuvaʻe ʻoʻona ʻoku ʻikai taau mo au ke u punou hifo ʻo vevete.
And preached, saying, There cometh one mightier than I after me, the latchet of whose shoes I am not worthy to stoop down and unloose.
Ko e moʻoni, kuo u papitaiso ʻaki ʻakimoutolu ʻae vai: ka te ne papitaiso ʻaki ʻakimoutolu ʻae Laumālie Māʻoniʻoni.”
I indeed have baptized you with water: but he shall baptize you with the Holy Ghost.
Pea ʻi he ngaahi ʻaho ko ia, naʻe haʻu ʻa Sisu mei Nāsaleti ʻo Kaleli, pea papitaiso ia ʻe Sione ʻi Sioatani.
And it came to pass in those days, that Jesus came from Nazareth of Galilee, and was baptized of John in Jordan.
Pea ʻalu hake leva ia mei he vai, pea ne mamata kuo mavaeua ʻae langi, pea maliu hifo ʻae Laumālie kiate ia, ʻo hangē ko e lupe:
And straightway coming up out of the water, he saw the heavens opened, and the Spirit like a dove descending upon him:
Pea ongo mai ʻae leʻo mei he langi, naʻe pehē, “Ko hoku ʻAlo ʻofaʻanga koe, ʻaia ʻoku ou fiemālie lahi ai.”
And there came a voice from heaven, saying, Thou art my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.
Pea taki leva ia ʻe he Laumālie ki he toafa.
And immediately the Spirit driveth him into the wilderness.
Pea naʻe ʻi he toafa ia ʻi he ʻaho ʻe fāngofulu, ʻo ʻahiʻahiʻi ʻe Sētane; pea naʻe ʻi ai mo ia ʻae fanga manu kai vao; kae tauhi ia ʻe he kau ʻāngelo.
And he was there in the wilderness forty days, tempted of Satan; and was with the wild beasts; and the angels ministered unto him.
Pea kuo fakahū ʻa Sione ki he fale fakapōpula, pea haʻu ʻa Sisu ki Kaleli, ʻo malangaʻaki ʻae ongoongolelei ʻoe puleʻanga ʻoe ʻOtua,
Now after that John was put in prison, Jesus came into Galilee, preaching the gospel of the kingdom of God,
‌ʻo ne pehē, “Kuo hokosia ʻae kuonga, pea ʻoku ofi ʻae puleʻanga ʻoe ʻOtua: mou fakatomala, pea tui ki he ongoongolelei.”
And saying, The time is fulfilled, and the kingdom of God is at hand: repent ye, and believe the gospel.
Pea ʻi heʻene hāʻele ʻi he matātahi ʻo Kaleli, naʻa ne mamata kia Saimone, mo ʻAnitelū ko hono tokoua, ʻoku na lafo ʻae kupenga ki tahi: he ko e ongo toutai ika ʻakinaua.
Now as he walked by the sea of Galilee, he saw Simon and Andrew his brother casting a net into the sea: for they were fishers.
Pea pehē ʻe Sisu kiate kinaua, “Mo muimui mai ʻiate au, pea te u ngaohi ʻakimoua ke mo toutai tangata.”
And Jesus said unto them, Come ye after me, and I will make you to become fishers of men.
Pea naʻa na liʻaki leva, hona kupenga, ʻo muimui ʻiate ia.
And straightway they forsook their nets, and followed him.
Pea ʻalu siʻi atu ia, mo ne mamata kia Semisi ko e foha ʻo Sepeti, mo Sione ko hono tokoua, naʻa na ʻi he vaka foki, ʻo pena honau kupenga.
And when he had gone a little farther thence, he saw James the son of Zebedee, and John his brother, who also were in the ship mending their nets.
Pea ne ui leva ʻakinaua: pea naʻa na liʻaki ʻena tamai ko Sepeti ʻi he vaka mo e kau ngāue kuo unga, ka na muimui ʻiate ia.
And straightway he called them: and they left their father Zebedee in the ship with the hired servants, and went after him.
Pea nau ō ki Kapaneume: pea hū leva ia ki he falelotu ʻi he ʻaho Sāpate, ʻo ne ako.
And they went into Capernaum; and straightway on the sabbath day he entered into the synagogue, and taught.
Pea nau ofo ʻi heʻene akonaki: he naʻa ne akonakiʻi ʻakinautolu ʻo taau mo ia ʻoku mālohi, ka naʻe ʻikai hangē ko e kau tangata tohi.
And they were astonished at his doctrine: for he taught them as one that had authority, and not as the scribes.
Pea naʻe ʻi honau falelotu ʻae tangata naʻe ʻiate ia ʻae laumālie ʻuli: pea kalanga leva ia,
And there was in their synagogue a man with an unclean spirit; and he cried out,
‌ʻo pehē, “E Sisu ʻo Nāsaleti, tuku ai pe; ko e hā ʻakimautolu kiate koe? Kuo ke haʻu ke fakaʻauha ʻakimautolu? ʻOku ou ʻilo koe, ko e tokotaha māʻoniʻoni ʻoe ʻOtua.”
Saying, Let us alone; what have we to do with thee, thou Jesus of Nazareth? art thou come to destroy us? I know thee who thou art, the Holy One of God.
Pea lolomi ia ʻe Sisu, ʻo pehē, “Ke ke fakalongo pē, pea ke haʻu kituʻa ʻiate ia.”
And Jesus rebuked him, saying, Hold thy peace, and come out of him.
Pea kuo haehae ia ʻe he laumālie ʻuli, mo tangi ʻaki ʻae leʻo lahi, pea ne toki mahuʻi ʻiate ia.
And when the unclean spirit had torn him, and cried with a loud voice, he came out of him.

Pea naʻe ofo ai ʻakinautolu kotoa pē, ko ia ne nau fakafefehuʻiʻaki ai ʻiate kinautolu, ʻo pehē, “Ko e hā ʻae meʻa ko eni? Ko e hā ʻae akonaki foʻou ni? He ʻoku fekau ʻe ia ʻi he mālohi ki he kau laumālie ʻuli, pea ʻoku nau talangofua kiate ia.”

And they were all amazed, insomuch that they questioned among themselves, saying, What thing is this? what new doctrine is this? for with authority commandeth he even the unclean spirits, and they do obey him.
Pea naʻe mafola leva ʻa hono ongoongo ʻi he potu kotoa pē ʻo Kaleli.
And immediately his fame spread abroad throughout all the region round about Galilee.
Pea kuo nau ʻalu mei he falelotu, naʻa nau hū, fakataha mo Semisi mo Sione, ki he fale ʻo Saimone mo ʻAnitelū.
And forthwith, when they were come out of the synagogue, they entered into the house of Simon and Andrew, with James and John.
Ka naʻe tokoto ʻae faʻē ʻae uaifi ʻo Saimone ʻoku mahaki ko e mofi; pea nau fakahā leva ia kiate ia.
But Simon’s wife’s mother lay sick of a fever, and anon they tell him of her.
Pea haʻu ia ʻo puke hono nima, ʻo ne fokotuʻu ia: pea mahuʻi leva ʻae mofi ʻiate ia, ʻo ne tauhi ʻakinautolu.
And he came and took her by the hand, and lifted her up; and immediately the fever left her, and she ministered unto them.
Pea kuo efiafi, ʻo feʻunga mo e tō ʻae laʻā, mo ʻenau ʻomi kiate ia ʻakinautolu kotoa pē naʻe mahaki, mo kinautolu naʻe ulusino ai ʻae kau tēvolo.
And at even, when the sun did set, they brought unto him all that were diseased, and them that were possessed with devils.
Pea fakataha ʻae kolo kotoa pē ki he matapā.
And all the city was gathered together at the door.
Pea fakamoʻui ʻe ia ʻae tokolahi naʻe mahaki ʻi he mahaki kehekehe, mo ne kapusi ʻae kau tēvolo tokolahi: pea ne taʻofi ke ʻoua ʻe lea ʻae kau tēvolo, koeʻuhi kuo nau ʻilo ia.
And he healed many that were sick of divers diseases, and cast out many devils; and suffered not the devils to speak, because they knew him.
Pea pongipongi ai, naʻa ne tuʻu hake ʻoku teʻeki ʻaho, pea ʻalu ia kituaʻā ʻo mole atu ki he potu lala, pea lotu ai.
And in the morning, rising up a great while before day, he went out, and departed into a solitary place, and there prayed.
Pea muimui ʻiate ia ʻa Saimone, mo kinautolu naʻe ʻiate ia.
And Simon and they that were with him followed after him.
Pea kuo ʻilo ia, pea nau pehē kiate ia, “ʻOku kumi kotoa pē kiate koe.”
And when they had found him, they said unto him, All men seek for thee.
Pea pehē ʻe ia kiate kinautolu, “Ke tau ō ki he ngaahi potu kakai ʻoku ofi mai, koeʻuhi ke u malanga ai foki: he ko ia naʻaku haʻu ai.”
And he said unto them, Let us go into the next towns, that I may preach there also: for therefore came I forth.
Pea naʻe ʻalu ʻo malanga ʻe ia ʻi honau ngaahi falelotu ʻi Kāleli kotoa pē, mo ne kapusi ʻae kau tēvolo.
And he preached in their synagogues throughout all Galilee, and cast out devils.
Pea naʻe haʻu kiate ia ʻae kilia, naʻe kole kiate ia, ʻo tuʻulutui kiate ia, mo ne pehē kiate ia, “Kapau ko ho finangalo ʻoku ke faʻa fakamaʻa au.”
And there came a leper to him, beseeching him, and kneeling down to him, and saying unto him, If thou wilt, thou canst make me clean.
Pea ʻaloʻofa ʻa Sisu, ʻo mafao atu hono nima, ʻo ala kiate ia, pea ne pehē ki ai, “Ko hoku loto ia; ke ke maʻa koe.”
And Jesus, moved with compassion, put forth his hand, and touched him, and saith unto him, I will; be thou clean.
Pea kuo lea ia, mo ʻene mahuʻi leva ʻae kilia ʻiate ia, pea maʻa ai ia.
And as soon as he had spoken, immediately the leprosy departed from him, and he was cleansed.
Pea ne naʻinaʻi mālohi kiate ia, pea toki fekau ke ne ʻalu:
And he straitly charged him, and forthwith sent him away;

‌ʻo ne pehē ki ai, “Vakai ʻoua naʻa ke lea ki ha taha: ka ke ʻalu, ʻo fakahā Ko e ki he taulaʻeiki, mo ʻatu ʻae ngaahi meʻa naʻe fekau ʻe Mōsese koeʻuhi ko hoʻo fakamaʻa, ko e fakamoʻoni kiate kinautolu.”
And saith unto him, See thou say nothing to any man: but go thy way, shew thyself to the priest, and offer for thy cleansing those things which Moses commanded, for a testimony unto them.

Ka naʻe ʻalu atu ia, ʻo ne kamata fakahā ʻo lahi, mo fanongonongo ʻae meʻa ni, ko ia naʻe ʻikai ai ke toe faʻa ʻalu fakahā ʻa Sisu ʻi he kolo, ka naʻe ʻi tuaʻā ia ʻi he ngaahi potu lala: pea naʻa nau haʻu mei he potu kotoa pē kiate ia.

But he went out, and began to publish it much, and to blaze abroad the matter, insomuch that Jesus could no more openly enter into the city, but was without in desert places: and they came to him from every quarter.
Pea hili ʻae ngaahi ʻaho pea toe ʻalu ia ki Kapaneume; pea kuo ongo atu ʻoku ʻi he fale ia.
And again he entered into Capernaum after some days; and it was noised that he was in the house.
Pea fakataha leva ʻae fuʻu tokolahi, naʻe ʻikai ke faʻa hao ʻi he fale, pe ofi ki he matapā: pea malangaʻaki ʻe ia ʻae folofola kiate kinautolu.
And straightway many were gathered together, insomuch that there was no room to receive them, no, not so much as about the door: and he preached the word unto them.
Pea naʻe ʻomi mo kinautolu kiate ia ʻae tokotaha naʻe mahaki tete, ʻaia naʻe fata ʻe he toko fā.
And they come unto him, bringing one sick of the palsy, which was borne of four.

Pea ʻi he ʻikai te nau faʻa hao ʻo ofi kiate ia koeʻuhi ko e kakai, naʻa nau tatala ʻae ʻato ʻoe fale naʻe ʻi ai ia: pea kuo haeʻi ia, naʻa nau tukutuku hifo ʻae mohenga naʻe tokoto ai ʻae mahaki tete.
And when they could not come nigh unto him for the press, they uncovered the roof where he was: and when they had broken it up, they let down the bed wherein the sick of the palsy lay.
Pea kuo mamata ʻa Sisu ki heʻenau tui, pea pehē ʻe ia ki he mahaki tete, “Foha, kuo fakamolemole hoʻo ngaahi angahala.”
When Jesus saw their faith, he said unto the sick of the palsy, Son, thy sins be forgiven thee.
Ka naʻe nofo ai ʻae niʻihi ʻoe kau tangata tohi, ʻonau fifili ʻi honau loto, ʻo pehē,
But there were certain of the scribes sitting there, and reasoning in their hearts,
“Ko e hā ʻoku lea fie ʻOtua pehē ai ʻae tangata ni? Ko hai ʻe faʻa fakamolemole ʻae angahala ka ko e ʻOtua pe?”
Why doth this man thus speak blasphemies? who can forgive sins but God only?
Pea kuo ʻiloʻi leva ʻe Sisu ʻi hono loto ʻoku pehē ʻenau fifili ʻi honau loto, pea pehē ʻe ia kiate kinautolu, “Ko e hā ʻoku mou fifili ai ʻi homou loto ki he ngaahi meʻa ni?
And immediately when Jesus perceived in his spirit that they so reasoned within themselves, he said unto them, Why reason ye these things in your hearts?
He ʻoku faingofua ʻa fē, ʻae lea ʻaki ki he mahaki tete, ‘Kuo fakamolemole hoʻo ngaahi angahala;’ pe ko e lea, ‘Tuʻu hake, ʻo toʻo ho mohenga, mo ke ʻalu?’
Whether is it easier to say to the sick of the palsy, Thy sins be forgiven thee; or to say, Arise, and take up thy bed, and walk?
Ka koeʻuhi ke mou ʻilo ʻoku ʻi he Foha ʻoe tangata ʻae mālohi ʻi māmani ke fakamolemole ʻae angahala,” (pea pehē ʻe ia ki he mahaki tete),
But that ye may know that the Son of man hath power on earth to forgive sins, (he saith to the sick of the palsy,)
“ʻOku ou pehē atu kiate koe, Tuʻu hake, ʻo toʻo ho mohenga, mo ke ʻalu ki ho fale.”
I say unto thee, Arise, and take up thy bed, and go thy way into thine house.

Pea tuʻu hake leva ia, ʻo toʻo ʻae mohenga, pea ne ʻalu kituʻa ʻi he ʻao ʻokinautolu kotoa pē; ko ia ne nau ofo ai kotoa pē, mo fakamālō ki he ʻOtua, ʻonau pehē, “Kuo teʻeki te tau mamata ʻi ha meʻa pehē.”
And immediately he arose, took up the bed, and went forth before them all; insomuch that they were all amazed, and glorified God, saying, We never saw it on this fashion.
Pea toe ʻalu atu ia ki he matātahi; pea kātoa kiate ia ʻae kakai kotoa pē, pea ne akonakiʻi ʻakinautolu.
And he went forth again by the sea side; and all the multitude resorted unto him, and he taught them.
Pea ʻi heʻene ʻalu atu, naʻa ne mamata kia Livai ko e foha ʻo ʻAlefiusi, ʻoku nofo ia ʻi he tukuhauʻanga, pea ne pehē kiate ia, “Muimui kiate au.” Pea tuʻu ia ʻo muimui ʻiate ia.
And as he passed by, he saw Levi the son of Alphaeus sitting at the receipt of custom, and said unto him, Follow me. And he arose and followed him.
Pea ʻi he nofo ʻa Sisu ʻi hono fale, ʻo kai, naʻe tokolahi ʻae tānaki tukuhau mo e angahala, naʻa nau nonofo mo Sisu mo ʻene kau ākonga: he naʻe tokolahi ʻakinautolu naʻe muimui ʻiate ia.
And it came to pass, that, as Jesus sat at meat in his house, many publicans and sinners sat also together with Jesus and his disciples: for there were many, and they followed him.

Pea ʻi he mamata ʻe he kau tangata tohi mo e Fālesi ʻoku ne kai mo e kau tānaki tukuhau mo e angahala, naʻa nau pehē ki heʻene kau ākonga, “Ko e hā ʻoku kai mo inu fakataha ai ia mo e kau tānaki tukuhau mo e angahala?”
And when the scribes and Pharisees saw him eat with publicans and sinners, they said unto his disciples, How is it that he eateth and drinketh with publicans and sinners?

Pea kuo fanongo ʻa Sisu ki ai, pea pehē ʻe ia kiate kinautolu, “ʻOku ʻikai ʻaonga ʻae faitoʻo kiate kinautolu ʻoku mālōlō, ka ki he mahaki: naʻe ʻikai teu haʻu ke ui ʻae māʻoniʻoni, ka ko e angahala ke fakatomala.”
When Jesus heard it, he saith unto them, They that are whole have no need of the physician, but they that are sick: I came not to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.

Pea naʻe faʻa ʻaukai ʻae kau ākonga ʻa Sione mo e ākonga ʻae kau Fālesi: pea nau haʻu ʻo pehē kiate ia, “Ko e hā ʻoku faʻa ʻaukai ai ʻae kau ākonga ʻa Sione pea mo e Fālesi, ka ʻoku ʻikai ʻaukai hoʻo kau ākonga?”
And the disciples of John and of the Pharisees used to fast: and they come and say unto him, Why do the disciples of John and of the Pharisees fast, but thy disciples fast not?

Pea pehē ʻe Sisu kiate kinautolu, “E faʻa ʻaukai ʻae kāinga ʻoe tangata taʻane, ʻi he kei ʻiate kinautolu ʻae tangata taʻane? E ʻikai te nau faʻa ʻaukai ʻi he lolotonga ʻoku ʻiate kinautolu ʻae tangata taʻane.
And Jesus said unto them, Can the children of the bridechamber fast, while the bridegroom is with them? as long as they have the bridegroom with them, they cannot fast.
Kae hoko ʻae ngaahi ʻaho ʻe ʻave ai ʻiate kinautolu ʻae tangata taʻane, pea ko e ngaahi ʻaho ko ia te nau toki ʻaukai ai.
But the days will come, when the bridegroom shall be taken away from them, and then shall they fast in those days.
“ʻOku ʻikai foki ha taha te ne ʻai ha konga meʻa foʻou ki he kofu motuʻa: he ko e konga foʻou ʻoku ʻai ke ʻoposi ʻaki, ʻe mafaufau ai ia pea ʻe ʻāsili ai hono mahaehae.
No man also seweth a piece of new cloth on an old garment: else the new piece that filled it up taketh away from the old, and the rent is made worse.

Pea ʻoku ʻikai utu ʻeha taha ʻae uaine foʻou ki he ngaahi hina ʻoku motuʻa; ka pehē ʻe haeʻi ʻe he uaine foʻou ʻae ngaahi hina, pea malingi ʻae uaine, pea maumau ʻae hina; ka ʻoku ʻutu ʻae uaine foʻou ki he ngaahi hina foʻou.”
And no man putteth new wine into old bottles: else the new wine doth burst the bottles, and the wine is spilled, and the bottles will be marred: but new wine must be put into new bottles.
Pea naʻe ʻalu ia ʻi he ngaahi ngoue uite ʻi he ʻaho Sāpate; pea ʻi heʻenau ʻalu, naʻe kamata toli ʻe heʻene kau ākonga ʻae fua ʻoe uite.
And it came to pass, that he went through the corn fields on the sabbath day; and his disciples began, as they went, to pluck the ears of corn.
Pea pehē ʻe he kau Fālesi kiate ia, “Vakai, ko e hā ʻoku nau fai ai ʻi he ʻaho Sāpate ʻaia ʻoku ʻikai ngofua?”
And the Pharisees said unto him, Behold, why do they on the sabbath day that which is not lawful?
Pea pehē ʻe ia kiate kinautolu, “Naʻe ʻikai te mou lau ʻaia naʻe fai ʻe Tevita, ʻi heʻene tuʻutāmaki, mo fiekaia, ʻaia mo kinautolu naʻe ʻiate ia?
And he said unto them, Have ye never read what David did, when he had need, and was an hungred, he, and they that were with him?

‌ʻA ʻene hū ki he fale ʻoe ʻOtua ʻi he ngaahi ʻaho ʻo ʻApiata ko e taulaʻeiki lahi, ʻo ne kai ʻae mā ʻoe ʻao, ʻaia naʻe ʻikai ngofua ke kai ka ko e kau taulaʻeiki pe, pea ne ʻange foki kiate kinautolu naʻe ʻiate ia?
How he went into the house of God in the days of Abiathar the high priest, and did eat the shewbread, which is not lawful to eat but for the priests, and gave also to them which were with him?
Pea pehē ʻe ia kiate kinautolu, Naʻe ngaohi ʻae Sāpate koeʻuhi ko e tangata, ka naʻe ʻikai ngaohi ʻae tangata koeʻuhi ko e Sāpate:
And he said unto them, The sabbath was made for man, and not man for the sabbath:
ko ia ko e Foha ʻoe tangata ko e ʻEiki ia ʻoe Sāpate foki.”
Therefore the Son of man is Lord also of the sabbath.
Pea toe hū ia ki he falelotu; pea naʻe ʻi ai ʻae tangata kuo mate hono nima.
And he entered again into the synagogue; and there was a man there which had a withered hand.
Pea naʻa nau lamasi ia, pe te ne fakamoʻui ia ʻi he ʻaho Sāpate: ka nau fakakoviʻi ai ia.
And they watched him, whether he would heal him on the sabbath day; that they might accuse him.
Pea pehē ʻe ia ki he tangata naʻe nima mate, “Tuʻu mai.”
And he saith unto the man which had the withered hand, Stand forth.
Pea ne pehē kiate kinautolu, “ʻOku ngofua ke fai lelei ʻi he ngaahi ʻaho Sāpate, pe ko e fai kovi? Ke fakamoʻui, pe tāmateʻi?” Ka naʻa nau fakalongo pe.
And he saith unto them, Is it lawful to do good on the sabbath days, or to do evil? to save life, or to kill? But they held their peace.

Pea kuo vakai foli ʻe ia ʻakinautolu kuo tuputāmaki, he naʻe mamahi ia koeʻuhi ko e fefeka ʻo honau loto, pea ne pehē ki he tangata, “Mafao mai ho nima.” Pea ne mafao atu ia: pea fakamoʻui hono nima ʻo hangē ko hono nima e taha.

And when he had looked round about on them with anger, being grieved for the hardness of their hearts, he saith unto the man, Stretch forth thine hand. And he stretched it out: and his hand was restored whole as the other.
Pea naʻe ʻalu kituʻa ʻae kau Fālesi, ʻonau alea leva mo e kau Helotiane kiate ia, pe fēfeeʻi ʻenau tāmateʻi ia.
And the Pharisees went forth, and straightway took counsel with the Herodians against him, how they might destroy him.
Ka naʻe ʻalu ʻa Sisu mo ʻene kau ākonga ki he tahi: pea muimui kiate ia ʻae fuʻu tokolahi mei Kāleli mo Siutea,
But Jesus withdrew himself with his disciples to the sea: and a great multitude from Galilee followed him, and from Judaea,
Pea naʻe haʻu kiate ia, mei Selūsalema, mo ʻAitumia, mo e tuʻa Sioatani, mo kinautolu naʻe ofi ki Taia mo Saitoni, ʻae fuʻu tokolahi ʻi heʻenau fanongo ki he ngaahi meʻa lahi kuo ne fai.
And from Jerusalem, and from Idumaea, and from beyond Jordan; and they about Tyre and Sidon, a great multitude, when they had heard what great things he did, came unto him.
Pea naʻe fekau ʻe ia ki heʻene kau ākonga, ke ʻai ha vaka siʻi ke tatali kiate ia, koeʻuhi ko e fuʻu tokolahi, telia naʻa nau fakaʻefihiaʻi ia.
And he spake to his disciples, that a small ship should wait on him because of the multitude, lest they should throng him.
He kuo ne fakamoʻui ʻae tokolahi; ko ia ne nau fakaʻefihiaʻi ia, ka nau ala kiate ia, ʻakinautolu naʻe mahaki.
For he had healed many; insomuch that they pressed upon him for to touch him, as many as had plagues.
Pea mo e kau laumālie ʻuli, ʻi heʻenau mamata kiate ia, naʻa nau tō ki lalo ʻi hono ʻao, pea tangi, ʻo pehē, “Ko e ʻAlo koe ʻoe ʻOtua.”
And unclean spirits, when they saw him, fell down before him, and cried, saying, Thou art the Son of God.
Pea ne fekau mālohi kiate kinautolu, ke ʻoua naʻa nau fakahā ia.
And he straitly charged them that they should not make him known.
Pea naʻe ʻalu hake ia ki he moʻunga, ʻo ne ui kiate ia ʻakinautolu naʻe loto ia ki ai: pea nau ʻalu ange kiate ia.
And he goeth up into a mountain, and calleth unto him whom he would: and they came unto him.
Pea ne tuʻutuʻuni ʻae toko hongofulu ma toko ua, ke nau ʻiate ia, pea koeʻuhi ke ne fekau atu ʻakinautolu ke malanga,
And he ordained twelve, that they should be with him, and that he might send them forth to preach,
Pea ke maʻu ʻae mālohi ke fakamoʻui ʻae ngaahi mahaki, mo kapusi ʻae kau tēvolo:
And to have power to heal sicknesses, and to cast out devils:
Ko Saimone naʻa ne fakahingoa ko Pita;
And Simon he surnamed Peter;
mo Semisi ko e foha ʻo Sepeti, mo Sione ko e tokoua ʻo Semisi; pea ne fakahingoa ʻakinaua ko Poaneasesi, ʻa ia, “Ko e ongo foha ʻoe mana:”
And James the son of Zebedee, and John the brother of James; and he surnamed them Boanerges, which is, The sons of thunder:
mo ʻAnitelū, mo Filipe, mo Pātolomiu, mo Mātiu, mo Tōmasi, mo Semisi ko e foha ʻo ʻAlefiusi, mo Tatiusi, mo Saimone ko e Kēnani,
And Andrew, and Philip, and Bartholomew, and Matthew, and Thomas, and James the son of Alphaeus, and Thaddaeus, and Simon the Canaanite,
mo Siutasi ʻIsikaliote ʻaia foki naʻa ne lavakiʻi ia: pea naʻa nau hū ki ha fale.
And Judas Iscariot, which also betrayed him: and they went into an house.
Pea toe fakataha ʻae kakai, ko ia naʻe ʻikai ai te nau faʻa fai ʻenau kai mā.
And the multitude cometh together again, so that they could not so much as eat bread.
Pea ʻi he fanongo ki ai ʻa hono kāinga, naʻa nau ʻalu atu ko hono puke: he naʻa nau pehē, “Kuo vale ia.”
And when his friends heard of it, they went out to lay hold on him: for they said, He is beside himself.
Pea naʻe pehē ʻe he kau tangata tohi naʻe ʻalu hifo mei Selūsalema, “ʻOku ʻiate ia ʻa Pelisipupe, pea ʻoku ne kapusi ʻae kau tēvolo ʻi he ʻeiki ʻoe kau tēvolo.”
And the scribes which came down from Jerusalem said, He hath Beelzebub, and by the prince of the devils casteth he out devils.
Pea ne ui ʻakinautolu, mo ne pehē kiate kinautolu ʻi he ngaahi fakatātā, “E faʻa kapusi fēfē ʻe Sētane ʻa Sētane?
And he called them unto him, and said unto them in parables, How can Satan cast out Satan?
Pea kapau ʻe feʻiteʻitani ha puleʻanga, ʻe ʻikai tuʻumaʻu ʻae puleʻanga ko ia.
And if a kingdom be divided against itself, that kingdom cannot stand.
Pea kapau ʻe feʻiteʻitani ha fale, ʻe ʻikai tuʻumaʻu ʻae fale ko ia.
And if a house be divided against itself, that house cannot stand.
Pea kapau ʻe angatuʻu ʻa Sētane kiate ia, mo feʻiteʻitani, ʻe ʻikai tuʻumaʻu ia, kae ngata ai ia.
And if Satan rise up against himself, and be divided, he cannot stand, but hath an end.
“E ʻikai ha taha te ne faʻa hū ki he fale ʻoe tokotaha mālohi, mo kaihaʻasi ʻene ngaahi koloa, ka ʻi heʻene tomuʻa haʻi ʻae tokotaha mālohi; pea te ne toki kaihaʻasi ʻene koloa.
No man can enter into a strong man’s house, and spoil his goods, except he will first bind the strong man; and then he will spoil his house.
“Ko e moʻoni ʻoku ou tala atu kiate kimoutolu, ʻE fakamolemole ʻae ngaahi hia kotoa pē ʻae fānau ʻae tangata, mo e lohiakiʻi ʻaia kotoa pē te nau lohiaki:
Verily I say unto you, All sins shall be forgiven unto the sons of men, and blasphemies wherewith soever they shall blaspheme:
Ka ko e lohiakiʻi ʻoe Laumālie Māʻoniʻoni ʻe ʻikai fakamolemolea ʻo lauikuonga, ka ʻoku tuʻutāmaki ia ki he malaʻia taʻengata:”
But he that shall blaspheme against the Holy Ghost hath never forgiveness, but is in danger of eternal damnation:
Koeʻuhi naʻe pehē ʻekinautolu, “ʻOku ʻiate ia ʻae laumālie ʻuli.”
Because they said, He hath an unclean spirit.
Pea naʻe toki haʻu ʻa hono kāinga mo ʻene faʻē, ʻonau tutuʻu ʻituʻa, pea nau fekau kiate ia.
There came then his brethren and his mother, and, standing without, sent unto him, calling him.
Pea pehē kiate ia ʻe he kakai naʻa nau nofo ʻo kāpui ia, “Vakai, ko hoʻo faʻē mo ho kāinga ʻoku ʻituʻa, ko ʻenau kumi koe.”
And the multitude sat about him, and they said unto him, Behold, thy mother and thy brethren without seek for thee.
Pea lea ia, ʻo pehēange kiate kinautolu, “Ko hai ʻeku faʻē mo hoku kāinga?”
And he answered them, saying, Who is my mother, or my brethren?
Pea vakai foli ʻe ia ʻakinautolu naʻa nau nofo ʻo kāpui ia, mo ne pehē, “Vakai, ko ʻeku faʻē mo hoku kāinga!
And he looked round about on them which sat about him, and said, Behold my mother and my brethren!
He ko ia te ne fai ʻae finangalo ʻoe ʻOtua, ko hoku tokoua ia, mo hoku tuofefine, mo ʻeku faʻē.”
For whosoever shall do the will of God, the same is my brother, and my sister, and mother.
Pea toe kamata akonaki ia ʻi he matātahi: pea kuo kātoa kiate ia ʻae fuʻu kakai, ko ia ne heka ai ia ki he vaka, ʻo nofo ʻi tahi: pea naʻe ʻi ʻuta ʻo ofi ki tahi ʻae kakai kotoa pē.
And he began again to teach by the sea side: and there was gathered unto him a great multitude, so that he entered into a ship, and sat in the sea; and the whole multitude was by the sea on the land.
Pea ne akonaki ʻaki ʻakinautolu ʻae meʻa kehekehe ʻi he fakatātā, ʻo ne pehē kiate kinautolu ʻi heʻene akonaki,
And he taught them many things by parables, and said unto them in his doctrine,
“Fanongo; Vakai, naʻe ʻalu atu ʻae tangata tūtuuʻi ke tūtuuʻi:
Hearken; Behold, there went out a sower to sow:
Pea ʻi heʻene tūtuuʻi, naʻe mokulu ʻa e tenga niʻihi ʻi he veʻe hala, pea haʻu ʻae fanga manupuna ʻoe ʻatā, ʻo kai ʻo ʻosi ia.
And it came to pass, as he sowed, some fell by the way side, and the fowls of the air came and devoured it up.
Pea mokulu ʻae niʻihi ki he potu makamaka, naʻe siʻi ai ʻae kelekele; pea tupu leva ia, koeʻuhi naʻe ʻikai matolu ʻae kelekele:
And some fell on stony ground, where it had not much earth; and immediately it sprang up, because it had no depth of earth:
Ka ʻi he ʻalu hake ʻae laʻā, naʻe vela ai ia; pea koeʻuhi naʻe ʻikai hano aka, ne mate ia.
But when the sun was up, it was scorched; and because it had no root, it withered away.
Pea mokulu ʻae niʻihi ki he ʻakau talatala, pea tupu hake ʻae ʻakau talatala, ʻo fakakāsia ia, pea ʻikai ai hano fua.
And some fell among thorns, and the thorns grew up, and choked it, and it yielded no fruit.
Pea mokulu ʻae niʻihi ki he kelekele lelei, pea tupu hake ʻae fua ʻo lahi; ʻo taki tolungofulu ʻae niʻihi, pea taki onongofulu ʻae niʻihi, pea taki teau ʻae niʻihi.”
And other fell on good ground, and did yield fruit that sprang up and increased; and brought forth, some thirty, and some sixty, and some an hundred.
Pea pehē ʻe ia kiate kinautolu, “Ko ia ʻoku telinga ongo, ke ongoʻi ia.”
And he said unto them, He that hath ears to hear, let him hear.
Pea kuo tokotaha pe ia, pea ko kinautolu naʻe ʻiate ia mo e toko hongofulu ma toko ua, naʻa nau fehuʻi kiate ia ki he fakatātā.
And when he was alone, they that were about him with the twelve asked of him the parable.
Pea pehē ʻe ia kiate kinautolu, “Kuo tuku kiate kimoutolu ke mou ʻilo ʻae meʻa lilo ʻoe puleʻanga ʻoe ʻOtua: ka ʻoku fai ʻae ngaahi meʻani kotoa pē ʻi he fakatātā kiate kinautolu ʻoku ʻituʻa:
And he said unto them, Unto you it is given to know the mystery of the kingdom of God: but unto them that are without, all these things are done in parables:
Koeʻuhi ‘ʻOku nau ʻā ʻo mamata, kae ʻikai ʻilo; pea ʻoku nau fanongo mo ongo, kae ʻikai tokanga; telia naʻa ʻiloange kuo liliu ai ʻakinautolu, pea fakamolemole ai ʻenau ngaahi hia.’”
That seeing they may see, and not perceive; and hearing they may hear, and not understand; lest at any time they should be converted, and their sins should be forgiven them.
Pea pehē ʻe ia kiate kinautolu, “ʻOku ʻikai te mou ʻilo ʻae fakatātā ni? Pea te mou ʻilo fēfē ʻae ngaahi fakatātā kotoa pē?
And he said unto them, Know ye not this parable? and how then will ye know all parables?
Ko e tangata tūtuuʻi ʻoku ne tūtuuʻi ʻae folofola.
The sower soweth the word.
Ko kinautolu eni ʻi he veʻe hala, ʻaia ʻoku tūtuuʻi ki ai ʻae folofola; pea kuo nau fanongo, pea haʻu leva ʻa Sētane, ʻo ʻave ʻae folofola naʻe tūtuuʻi ki honau loto.
And these are they by the way side, where the word is sown; but when they have heard, Satan cometh immediately, and taketh away the word that was sown in their hearts.
Pea ko kinautolu eni foki kuo tūtuuʻi ʻi he potu makaʻia; ʻi heʻenau fanongo ki he folofola ʻoku nau maʻu leva ia ʻi he fiefia;
And these are they likewise which are sown on stony ground; who, when they have heard the word, immediately receive it with gladness;
Ka ʻoku ʻikai ha aka ʻiate kinautolu, ko ia ʻoku nau maʻu ai ia ʻo fuonounou: pea ka tupu ʻae mamahi pe ʻae fakatanga, koeʻuhi ko e folofola, ʻoku hinga leva ʻakinautolu.
And have no root in themselves, and so endure but for a time: afterward, when affliction or persecution ariseth for the word’s sake, immediately they are offended.
Pea ko kinautolu eni kuo tūtuuʻi ki he ʻakau talatala; ʻoku nau fanongo ki he folofola,
And these are they which are sown among thorns; such as hear the word,
Ka ko e tokanga ki māmani, mo e kākā ʻoe koloa, mo e hū ʻae holi lahi ki he ngaahi meʻa kehekehe, ʻoku kāsia ai ʻae folofola, pea taʻefua ai ia.
And the cares of this world, and the deceitfulness of riches, and the lusts of other things entering in, choke the word, and it becometh unfruitful.

Pea ko kinautolu eni kuo tūtuuʻi ki he kelekele lelei; ʻoku nau fanongo ki he folofola, pea maʻu ia, pea tupu ai ʻae fua, ko e taki tolungofulu ʻae niʻihi, pea taki onongofulu ʻae niʻihi, pea taki teau ʻae niʻihi.”
And these are they which are sown on good ground; such as hear the word, and receive it, and bring forth fruit, some thirtyfold, some sixty, and some an hundred.
Pea pehē ʻe ia kiate kinautolu, “ʻOku ʻomi koā ha maama ke tuku ʻi he lalo puha fua, pe ʻi lalo mohenga? Kae ʻikai ke fokotuʻu ki he tuʻunga maama?
And he said unto them, Is a candle brought to be put under a bushel, or under a bed? and not to be set on a candlestick?
He ʻoku ʻikai ha meʻa ʻoku ʻufiʻufi, ʻe taʻefakahā; pea ʻoku ʻikai ha meʻa fakalilolilo, ʻe taʻeʻiloa.
For there is nothing hid, which shall not be manifested; neither was any thing kept secret, but that it should come abroad.
Ko e tangata ko ia ʻoku telinga ongo, ke ongoʻi ia.”
If any man have ears to hear, let him hear.
Pea pehē ʻe ia kiate kinautolu, “Tokanga ki he meʻa ʻoku mou fanongo ki ai: he ko e meʻa fuofua te mou fua ʻaki, ʻe toe fua ʻaki kiate kimoutolu: pea ʻe foaki fakalahi kiate kimoutolu ʻoku tokanga.
And he said unto them, Take heed what ye hear: with what measure ye mete, it shall be measured to you: and unto you that hear shall more be given.
He ko ia ʻoku ne maʻu, ʻe toe foaki kiate ia: pea ko ia ʻoku ʻikai ke maʻu, ʻe toʻo meiate ia ʻaia ʻoku ne maʻu.”
For he that hath, to him shall be given: and he that hath not, from him shall be taken even that which he hath.
Pea pehē ʻe ia, “Ko e puleʻanga ʻoe ʻOtua ʻoku tatau mo e tenga naʻe lī ʻe ha tangata ki he kelekele;
And he said, So is the kingdom of God, as if a man should cast seed into the ground;
Pea mohe ia, mo tuʻu hake, ʻi he pō mo e ʻaho, pea moʻui ʻae tenga ʻo tupu hake, ʻoku ʻikai te ne ʻilo pe ʻoku fēfē.
And should sleep, and rise night and day, and the seed should spring and grow up, he knoweth not how.
He ʻoku tupu ʻi he kelekele ʻae fua ʻoʻona pe; ko e ʻuluaki ko e muka, pea hoko mo e fua, pea toki hoko mo e uite kuo motuʻa.
For the earth bringeth forth fruit of herself; first the blade, then the ear, after that the full corn in the ear.
Pea ka motuʻa ʻae fua, ʻoku ne ʻai leva ʻae hele tuʻusi, koeʻuhi kuo hoko ʻae ututaʻu.
But when the fruit is brought forth, immediately he putteth in the sickle, because the harvest is come.
“Pea pehē ʻe ia, Te tau fakatatau ki he hā ʻae puleʻanga ʻoe ʻOtua? Pe ko e hā ha fakatātā te tau fakatatau ia ki ai?
And he said, Whereunto shall we liken the kingdom of God? or with what comparison shall we compare it?
‌ʻOku tatau ia mo e tengaʻi musita, ʻaia ʻoka tūtuuʻi ki he kelekele, ʻoku siʻi taha pe ʻi he ngaahi tenga kotoa pē ʻoku ʻi he kelekele:
It is like a grain of mustard seed, which, when it is sown in the earth, is less than all the seeds that be in the earth:
Ka kuo tūtuuʻi ia, pea tupu hake, ʻo hoko ʻo lahi ʻi he faʻahinga ʻakau iiki kotoa pē, pea tupu ia ʻo vaʻavaʻa lalahi: ko ia ʻoku faʻa nofo ʻae fanga manu ʻoe ʻatā ʻi hono malumalu.”
But when it is sown, it groweth up, and becometh greater than all herbs, and shooteth out great branches; so that the fowls of the air may lodge under the shadow of it.
Pea ʻi he ngaahi fakatātā pehē ʻo lahi, naʻa ne lea ʻaki ʻae lea kiate kinautolu, ʻo fakatatau ki heʻenau faʻa fanongo.
And with many such parables spake he the word unto them, as they were able to hear it.
Pea naʻe ʻikai te ne lea kiate kinautolu ka ʻi he fakatātā pe: pea ʻi heʻenau nonofo ko kinautolu pe, naʻa ne fakamatala ʻae meʻa kotoa pē ki heʻene kau ākonga.
But without a parable spake he not unto them: and when they were alone, he expounded all things to his disciples.
Pea kuo efiafi ʻi he ʻaho ko ia, naʻa ne pehē kiate kinautolu, “Ke tau ō ki he kauvai ʻe taha.”
And the same day, when the even was come, he saith unto them, Let us pass over unto the other side.
Pea kuo nau fekau ke ʻalu ʻae kakai, pea nau ʻave ia ʻi heʻene kei ʻi he vaka. Pea naʻe folau mo ia ʻae ngaahi vaka iiki.
And when they had sent away the multitude, they took him even as he was in the ship. And there were also with him other little ships.
Pea naʻe tupu ʻae fuʻu matangi lahi, pea feʻohofi ʻae ngaahi peau ki he vaka, pea ngoto ai.
And there arose a great storm of wind, and the waves beat into the ship, so that it was now full.
Pea naʻa ne ʻi he taumuli ʻoe vaka, ʻo mohe ki he ʻolunga: pea naʻa nau fafangu ia, ʻo pehē kiate ia, “ʻEiki, ʻoku ʻikai te ke tokangaʻi te tau mate?”
And he was in the hinder part of the ship, asleep on a pillow: and they awake him, and say unto him, Master, carest thou not that we perish?
Pea tuʻu hake ia, ʻo lolomi ʻae matangi, mo ne pehē ki he tahi, “Fiemālie, pea ke tokalelei.” Pea naʻe malū ʻae matangi, ʻo mātuʻaki tofukī.
And he arose, and rebuked the wind, and said unto the sea, Peace, be still. And the wind ceased, and there was a great calm.
Pea pehē ʻe ia kiate kinautolu, “Ko e hā ʻoku mou manavasiʻi pehē ai? Ko e hā ʻoku ʻikai ai haʻamou tui?”
And he said unto them, Why are ye so fearful? how is it that ye have no faith?
Pea naʻa nau manavahē lahi ʻaupito, mo nau fepehēʻaki, “Ko hai ʻae tangata ni, ke talangofua pehē ʻae matangi mo e tahi kiate ia?”
And they feared exceedingly, and said one to another, What manner of man is this, that even the wind and the sea obey him?
Pea naʻa nau tuku mai ki he kauvai ʻe taha ʻoe tahi, ki he fonua ʻoe kakai Kataline.
And they came over unto the other side of the sea, into the country of the Gadarenes.
Pea kuo haʻu ia mei he vaka, pea fakafetaulaki leva kiate ia ʻae tangata mei he ngaahi faʻitoka, pea naʻe ʻiate ia ʻae laumālie ʻuli,
And when he was come out of the ship, immediately there met him out of the tombs a man with an unclean spirit,
Pea naʻe nofo pe ia ʻi he ngaahi faʻitoka; pea naʻe ʻikai ha tangata te ne faʻa haʻi ʻaki ia ʻae ngaahi ukamea fihifihi:
Who had his dwelling among the tombs; and no man could bind him, no, not with chains:

He koeʻuhi kuo liunga lahi hono haʻi ʻaki ʻae ngaahi ukamea fakamaʻu mo e ngaahi ukamea fihifihi, pea kuo ne motumotuhi ʻae ngaahi ukamea fihifihi, pea motumotu mo e ngaahi ukamea fakamaʻu: pea kuo ʻikai faʻa fakalalata ia ʻe ha taha.
Because that he had been often bound with fetters and chains, and the chains had been plucked asunder by him, and the fetters broken in pieces: neither could any man tame him.
Pea naʻe ʻi he ngaahi moʻunga ia mo e ngaahi faʻitoka maʻuaipē, ʻi he pō mo e ʻaho, ʻo ne tangi ai, mo ne tafatafaʻi ʻaki ia ʻae ngaahi maka.
And always, night and day, he was in the mountains, and in the tombs, crying, and cutting himself with stones.
Ka ʻi heʻene mamata mei he mamaʻo kia Sisu, naʻa ne lele ʻo hū kiate ia.
But when he saw Jesus afar off, he ran and worshipped him,
‌ʻO tangi leʻo lahi, ʻo ne pehē, “Ko e hā au kiate koe, Sisu, ko e ʻAlo ʻoe fungani ʻOtua māʻolunga? ʻOku ou hū tōtōaki kiate koe ʻi he ʻOtua, ke ʻoua naʻa ke fakamamahiʻi au.”
And cried with a loud voice, and said, What have I to do with thee, Jesus, thou Son of the most high God? I adjure thee by God, that thou torment me not.
(He naʻa ne pehē kiate ia, “Haʻu kituʻa mei he tangata, ʻa koe ko e laumālie ʻuli.”)
For he said unto him, Come out of the man, thou unclean spirit.
Pea ne fehuʻi kiate ia, “Ko hai ho hingoa?” Pea pehēange ʻe ia, “Ko Lisione hoku hingoa; he ʻoku mau tokolahi.”
And he asked him, What is thy name? And he answered, saying, My name is Legion: for we are many.
Pea ne kole fakamātoato kiate ia ke ʻoua naʻa ne kapusi ʻakinautolu mei he fonua.
And he besought him much that he would not send them away out of the country.
Pea naʻe ʻi ai, ʻo ofi ki he ngaahi moʻunga, ʻae fanga puaka lahi naʻe fafanga.
Now there was there nigh unto the mountains a great herd of swine feeding.
Pea kole ʻe he kau laumālie kotoa pē kiate ia, ʻo pehē, “Fekau ʻakimautolu ki he fanga puaka, koeʻuhi ke mau hū ki ai.”
And all the devils besought him, saying, Send us into the swine, that we may enter into them.

Pea tuku leva ʻe Sisu ke nau fai ia. Pea ʻalu atu ʻae kau laumālie ʻuli, ʻo hū ki he fanga puaka: pea feleleʻi ʻo ʻoho ʻae fanga puaka ʻi he potu tahifohifo ki tahi, (naʻa nau toko ua afe nai;) pea melemo ʻi he tahi.

And forthwith Jesus gave them leave. And the unclean spirits went out, and entered into the swine: and the herd ran violently down a steep place into the sea, (they were about two thousand;) and were choked in the sea.
Pea feholaki ʻakinautolu naʻe tauhi ʻae fanga puaka, ʻo fakahā ki he kolo, pea mo e tukuʻuta. Pea naʻa nau ʻalu ange ke mamata ki he meʻa kuo fai.
And they that fed the swine fled, and told it in the city, and in the country. And they went out to see what it was that was done.
Pea nau haʻu kia Sisu, ʻo mamata kiate ia naʻe ulusino ai ʻae laumālie ʻuli, ʻo ne maʻu ʻae lisione, ʻoku nofo ia, kuo kofu, pea poto hono loto: pea nau manavahē
And they come to Jesus, and see him that was possessed with the devil, and had the legion, sitting, and clothed, and in his right mind: and they were afraid.
Pea ko kinautolu naʻe mamata ki ai, naʻa nau fakahā kiate kinautolu ʻae meʻa naʻe hoko kiate ia naʻe ulusino ai ʻae tēvolo, pea mo e meʻa ki he fanga puaka.
And they that saw it told them how it befell to him that was possessed with the devil, and also concerning the swine.
Pea nau kole leva kiate ia ke ne ʻalu ʻi honau fonua.
And they began to pray him to depart out of their coasts.
Pea kuo ʻalu ia ki vaka, pea ko ia naʻe ulusino ai ʻae tēvolo ne kole kiate ia ke na nonofo.
And when he was come into the ship, he that had been possessed with the devil prayed him that he might be with him.
Ka naʻe ʻikai loto ki ai ʻa Sisu, ka naʻa ne pehē, “ʻAlu ki ho ʻapi ki ho kāinga, mo fakahā kiate kinautolu ʻae ngaahi meʻa lahi kuo fai ʻe he ʻEiki maʻau, mo ʻene manavaʻofa kiate koe.”
Howbeit Jesus suffered him not, but saith unto him, Go home to thy friends, and tell them how great things the Lord hath done for thee, and hath had compassion on thee.
Pea ne ʻalu ia, ʻo fua fakahā ʻi Tikapolisi ʻae ngaahi meʻa lahi kuo fai ʻe Sisu maʻana: pea ofo ai kotoa pē.
And he departed, and began to publish in Decapolis how great things Jesus had done for him: and all men did marvel.
Pea kuo toe folau ʻa Sisu ʻi he vaka ki he kauvai ʻe taha, pea kātoa ai kiate ia ʻae kakai tokolahi: pea kuo ofi ia ki tahi.
And when Jesus was passed over again by ship unto the other side, much people gathered unto him: and he was nigh unto the sea.
Pea vakai, naʻe ʻalu ange ʻae tokotaha ʻoe kau pule ʻoe falelotu, ko Sailosi hono hingoa; pea ʻi heʻene mamata kiate ia, naʻa ne tō hifo ki hono vaʻe,
And, behold, there cometh one of the rulers of the synagogue, Jairus by name; and when he saw him, he fell at his feet,
‌ʻO ne kole fakamātoato kiate ia, ʻo pehē, “Ko hoku ʻofefine siʻi ʻoku tei mate: haʻu, ʻo hili ho nima kiate ia, koeʻuhi ke moʻui ai: pea ʻe moʻui ia.”
And besought him greatly, saying, My little daughter lieth at the point of death: I pray thee, come and lay thy hands on her, that she may be healed; and she shall live.
Pea naʻa na ō mo Sisu; pea muimui kiate ia ʻae kakai tokolahi, ʻo fakaʻefihia ia.
And Jesus went with him; and much people followed him, and thronged him.
Pea ko e fefine ʻe tokotaha, naʻe hongofulu ma ua ʻae taʻu ʻoe ʻau toto ʻiate ia,
And a certain woman, which had an issue of blood twelve years,
Pea kuo lahi ʻae meʻa kuo ne kātaki ʻi he kau faitoʻo tokolahi, pea kuo fakaʻosi ʻe ia ʻa ʻene meʻa kotoa pē, pea ʻikai fakaʻaʻau ki muʻa, kae ʻāsili pe hono mahaki.
And had suffered many things of many physicians, and had spent all that she had, and was nothing bettered, but rather grew worse,
Kuo fanongo ia kia Sisu, pea haʻu mo e fononga mei mui, ʻo ala ki hono kofu:
When she had heard of Jesus, came in the press behind, and touched his garment.
He kuo pehē ʻe ia, “Kapau teu ala pe ki hono kofu, te u moʻui ai.”
For she said, If I may touch but his clothes, I shall be whole.
Pea matuʻu fakafokifā pe ʻae ʻau ʻa hono toto; pea ne ongoʻi ʻi hono sino kuo fakamoʻui ia mei he mahaki ko ia.
And straightway the fountain of her blood was dried up; and she felt in her body that she was healed of that plague.
Pea kuo ʻilo loto ʻe Sisu kuo ʻalu atu ʻiate ia ʻae mālohi, pea ne tafoki ia ki he kakai, mo ne pehē, “Ko hai naʻe ala ki hoku kofu?”
And Jesus, immediately knowing in himself that virtue had gone out of him, turned him about in the press, and said, Who touched my clothes?
Pea pehēange ʻene kau ākonga kiate ia, “ʻOku ke vakai ki he tokolahi ʻoku fakaʻefi koe, pea ʻoku ke pehē, ‘Ko hai kuo ala kiate au?’”
And his disciples said unto him, Thou seest the multitude thronging thee, and sayest thou, Who touched me?
Pea vakai foli ʻe ia ke mamata kiate ia kuo ne fai ʻae meʻa ni.
And he looked round about to see her that had done this thing.
Ka kuo ʻilo ʻe he fefine ʻaia kuo fai kiate ia, pea haʻu ia, ʻoku manavahē mo tetetete, ʻo tō ki lalo ʻi hono ʻao, ʻo ne tala kiate ia ʻae moʻoni kotoa pē.
But the woman fearing and trembling, knowing what was done in her, came and fell down before him, and told him all the truth.
Pea ne pehē kiate ia, “ʻOfefine, kuo fakamoʻui koe ʻe hoʻo tui; ʻalu ʻi he fiemālie, pea ke moʻui mei hoʻo mahaki.”
And he said unto her, Daughter, thy faith hath made thee whole; go in peace, and be whole of thy plague.
Kae lolotonga ʻene lea, mo e haʻu ʻae niʻihi mei he fale ʻoe pule ʻoe falelotu, ʻonau pehē, “Kuo pekia ho ʻofefine: ko e hā ʻoku ke kei fakafiu ai ʻae ʻEiki?”
While he yet spake, there came from the ruler of the synagogue’s house certain which said, Thy daughter is dead: why troublest thou the Master any further?
Pea kuo fanongo leva ʻe Sisu ki he lea naʻe lea ʻaki, pea pehē ʻe ia ki he pule ʻoe falelotu, “ʻOua te ke manavahē, ka ke tui pe.”
As soon as Jesus heard the word that was spoken, he saith unto the ruler of the synagogue, Be not afraid, only believe.
Pea naʻe ʻikai tuku ʻe ia ke muimui ha tokotaha kiate ia, ka ko Pita, mo Semisi, mo Sione ko e tokoua ʻo Semisi.
And he suffered no man to follow him, save Peter, and James, and John the brother of James.
Pea hoko ia ki he fale ʻoe pule ʻoe falelotu, ʻo mamata ki he maveuveu, mo kinautolu naʻe tangi mo tangilāulau lahi.
And he cometh to the house of the ruler of the synagogue, and seeth the tumult, and them that wept and wailed greatly.
Pea kuo hū ia ki loto fale, mo ne pehē kiate kinautolu, “Ko e hā ʻoku mou maveuveu, mo tangi ai? ʻOku ʻikai mate ʻae taʻahine, ka ʻoku mohe pe.”
And when he was come in, he saith unto them, Why make ye this ado, and weep? the damsel is not dead, but sleepeth.

Ka naʻa nau kakata manuki kiate ia. Pea kuo fekau ʻe ia ke nau ʻalu kotoa pē kituʻa, pea ne ʻave ʻae tamai mo e faʻē ʻae taʻahine, mo kinautolu naʻe ʻiate ia, pea nau hū ki he potu ʻoku tokoto ai ʻae taʻahine.
And they laughed him to scorn. But when he had put them all out, he taketh the father and the mother of the damsel, and them that were with him, and entereth in where the damsel was lying.
Pea ne puke ʻae nima ʻoe taʻahine, mo ne pehē kiate ia, “Talita kiumi;” ʻaia ko hono ʻuhinga, “Taʻahine, ʻoku ou pehē kiate koe, Tuʻu hake.”
And he took the damsel by the hand, and said unto her, Talitha cumi; which is, being interpreted, Damsel, I say unto thee, arise.
Pea tuʻu hake leva ʻae taʻahine, ʻo ʻeveʻeva; he kuo hongofulu ma ua hono taʻu. Pea naʻe ofo ai ʻakinautolu ʻi he ofo lahi.
And straightway the damsel arose, and walked; for she was of the age of twelve years. And they were astonished with a great astonishment.
Pea ne fekau mālohi kiate kinautolu ke ʻoua naʻa ʻilo ia ʻe ha taha; mo ne fekau ke ʻatu ha meʻakai kiate ia.
And he charged them straitly that no man should know it; and commanded that something should be given her to eat.
Pea naʻe ʻalu ia mei ai, ʻo haʻu ki hono fonua; pea muimui ʻa ʻene kau ākonga kiate ia.
And he went out from thence, and came into his own country; and his disciples follow him.

Pea hokosia ʻae ʻaho Sāpate, pea kamata ako ia ʻi he falelotu; pea ofo ʻae tokolahi ʻi he fanongo kiate ia, ʻonau pehē, “Kuo maʻu mei fē ʻe he tangata ni ʻae ngaahi meʻa ni? Pea ko e hā ʻae poto ko eni kuo tuku kiate ia, ʻaia kuo fai ai ʻe hono nima ʻae ngaahi ngāue lahi pehē?

And when the sabbath day was come, he began to teach in the synagogue: and many hearing him were astonished, saying, From whence hath this man these things? and what wisdom is this which is given unto him, that even such mighty works are wrought by his hands?
‌ʻIkai ko e tufunga eni, ko e tama ʻa Mele, pea ko e tokoua ʻo Semisi, mo Sose, mo Siute, mo Saimone? Pea ʻikai ʻoku ʻi heni mo kitautolu ʻa hono ngaahi tuofefine?” Pea naʻa nau tūkia ʻiate ia.
Is not this the carpenter, the son of Mary, the brother of James, and Joses, and of Juda, and Simon? and are not his sisters here with us? And they were offended at him.
Ka naʻe pehē ʻe Sisu kiate kinautolu, “ʻOku ʻikai ke masiva fakaʻapaʻapa ha palōfita, ka ʻi hono fonua, mo hono kāinga, mo hono fale.”
But Jesus said unto them, A prophet is not without honour, but in his own country, and among his own kin, and in his own house.
Pea naʻe ʻikai te ne mafai ʻi ai ha ngāue lahi, ka naʻa ne hilifaki hono nima ki he tokosiʻi pe naʻe mahaki, ʻo ne fakamoʻui.
And he could there do no mighty work, save that he laid his hands upon a few sick folk, and healed them.
Pea naʻe ofo ia ko e meʻa ʻi heʻenau taʻetui. Pea ʻalu fakatakamilo ia ʻi he ngaahi potu kakai, ʻo akonaki.
And he marvelled because of their unbelief. And he went round about the villages, teaching.
Pea ne ui ʻae toko hongofulu ma toko ua, ʻo ne fua fekau ke nau ō, ʻo tautau toko ua, pea ne foaki kiate kinautolu ʻae mālohi ki he kau laumālie ʻuli;
And he called unto him the twelve, and began to send them forth by two and two; and gave them power over unclean spirits;
Mo fekau ʻe ia kiate kinautolu ke ʻoua te nau ʻave he meʻa ʻi honau fononga, ka ko e tokotoko pe; ʻoua naʻa ʻai ha kato, pe ha mā, pe ha paʻanga ʻi he noʻo:
And commanded them that they should take nothing for their journey, save a staff only; no scrip, no bread, no money in their purse:
Kae topuvaʻe ʻai ʻae teka; pea ʻoua naʻa ʻaki ʻae kofutuʻa ʻe ua.
But be shod with sandals; and not put on two coats.
Pea ne pehē kiate kinautolu, “Ko e potu ko ia te mou hū ai ki ha fale, mou nofo ai pe kaeʻoua ke mou toki ō ʻi he potu ko ia.
And he said unto them, In what place soever ye enter into an house, there abide till ye depart from that place.

Pea ko kinautolu ʻe ʻikai maʻu ʻakimoutolu, pe fanongo kiate kimoutolu, ʻoka mou ka ʻalu ai, mou tūtuuʻi ʻae efu ʻi homou vaʻe, ko e fakamoʻoni kiate kinautolu. Ko e moʻoni ʻoku ou tala kiate kimoutolu, ʻE kātakingofua ʻa Sotoma mo Komola ʻi he ʻaho fakamaau, ʻi he kolo ko ia.”

And whosoever shall not receive you, nor hear you, when ye depart thence, shake off the dust under your feet for a testimony against them. Verily I say unto you, It shall be more tolerable for Sodom and Gomorrha in the day of judgment, than for that city.
Pea naʻa nau ʻalu atu, ʻo malanga ke fakatomala ʻae kakai.
And they went out, and preached that men should repent.
Pea nau kapusi ʻae kau tēvolo tokolahi, pea tākai ʻaki ʻae lolo, mo fakamoʻui ʻae tokolahi naʻe mahaki.
And they cast out many devils, and anointed with oil many that were sick, and healed them.
Pea fanongo ki ai ʻae tuʻi ko Helota; (he kuo mafola atu hono hingoa;) pea pehē ʻe ia, Kuo toe tuʻu mei he mate ʻa Sione ko e Papitaiso, pea ko ia ʻoku hā ai ʻae ngaahi ngāue lahi meiate ia.
And king Herod heard of him; (for his name was spread abroad:) and he said, That John the Baptist was risen from the dead, and therefore mighty works do shew forth themselves in him.
Pea pehē ʻe he niʻihi, “Ko ʻIlaisiā ia.” Pea pehē ʻe he niʻihi, “Ko e palōfita ia, pe ʻoku hangē ko ha taha ʻi he kau palōfita.”
Others said, That it is Elias. And others said, That it is a prophet, or as one of the prophets.
Ka ʻi he fanongo ki ai ʻa Helota, pea pehē ʻe ia, “Ko Sione ia, ʻaia ne u tutuʻu hono ʻulu: kuo toe tuʻu ia mei he mate.”
But when Herod heard thereof, he said, It is John, whom I beheaded: he is risen from the dead.
He naʻe fekau atu ʻe Helota, ke puke ʻa Sione, ʻo haʻi ia ʻi he fale fakapōpula, ko e meʻa ia Helotiasi, ko e uaifi ʻo hono tokoua ko Filipe: he kuo na fakamaʻu mo ia.
For Herod himself had sent forth and laid hold upon John, and bound him in prison for Herodias’ sake, his brother Philip’s wife: for he had married her.
He naʻe pehē ʻe Sione kia Helota, “ʻOku ʻikai ngofua haʻo maʻu ʻae uaifi ʻo ho tokoua.”
For John had said unto Herod, It is not lawful for thee to have thy brother’s wife.
Ko ia naʻe ʻita ʻa Helotiasi kiate ia, ʻo ne loto ke tāmateʻi ia; ka naʻe ʻikai ke ne mafai ia:
Therefore Herodias had a quarrel against him, and would have killed him; but she could not:

He naʻe manavahē ʻa Helota kia Sione, ko ʻene ʻilo ko e tangata angatonu ia, mo māʻoniʻoni, pea naʻa ne maluʻi ia; pea ʻi heʻene fanongo kiate ia, naʻa ne fai ʻae ngaahi meʻa lahi, mo ne fanongo ʻi he fiefia.
For Herod feared John, knowing that he was a just man and an holy, and observed him; and when he heard him, he did many things, and heard him gladly.
Pea naʻe hokosia ʻae ʻaho lelei, ko e ʻaho fakamanatu ki he fanauʻi ʻo Helota, pea ne fai ai ʻae kātoanga mā ʻa hono ngaahi houʻeiki, mo e ngaahi ʻeikitau, mo e ngaahi ʻeiki ʻo Kāleli;
And when a convenient day was come, that Herod on his birthday made a supper to his lords, high captains, and chief estates of Galilee;

Pea kuo haʻu ki ai ʻae taʻahine ʻae Helotiasi ko ia, ʻo meʻe, pea mālieʻia ai ʻa Helota mo kinautolu naʻa nau nonofo, pea pehē ʻe he tuʻi ki he taʻahine, “Kole mai kiate au ʻaia ʻoku ke loto ki ai, pea te u foaki ia kiate koe.”
And when the daughter of the said Herodias came in, and danced, and pleased Herod and them that sat with him, the king said unto the damsel, Ask of me whatsoever thou wilt, and I will give it thee.
Pea ne fuakava kiate ia, “Ka ʻilonga ha meʻa te ke kole kiate au, te u foaki ia kiate koe, ʻo aʻu ki hono vaeua mālie ʻo hoku puleʻanga.”
And he sware unto her, Whatsoever thou shalt ask of me, I will give it thee, unto the half of my kingdom.
Pea ʻalu atu ia, ʻo ne pehē ki heʻene faʻē, “Ko e hā te u kole?” Pea pehēange ʻe ia, “Ko e ʻulu ʻo Sione ko e Papitaiso.”
And she went forth, and said unto her mother, What shall I ask? And she said, The head of John the Baptist.
Pea toe haʻu leva ia ki he tuʻi, pea ne kole, ʻo pehē, “Ko hoku loto ke ke foaki mai kiate au ʻanaiange, ʻae ʻulu ʻo Sione ko e Papitaiso, ʻi ha ipu.”
And she came in straightway with haste unto the king, and asked, saying, I will that thou give me by and by in a charger the head of John the Baptist.
Pea mamahi lahi ʻae tuʻi; ka ko e meʻa ʻi heʻene fuakava, pea koeʻuhi ko kinautolu naʻa nau nonofo mo ia, naʻe ʻikai te ne faʻa fakafisi kiate ia.
And the king was exceeding sorry; yet for his oath’s sake, and for their sakes which sat with him, he would not reject her.
Pea kouna leva ʻe he tuʻi ʻae tangata tāmate, ʻo fekau ke ʻomi hono ʻulu: pea ʻalu ia, ʻo tutuʻu hono ʻulu ʻi he fale fakapōpula,
And immediately the king sent an executioner, and commanded his head to be brought: and he went and beheaded him in the prison,
‌ʻo ne ʻomi hono ʻulu ʻi ha ipu, mo ʻatu ki he taʻahine: pea ʻange ia ʻe he taʻahine ki heʻene faʻē.
And brought his head in a charger, and gave it to the damsel: and the damsel gave it to her mother.
Pea ʻi he fanongo ki ai ʻa ʻene kau ākonga, naʻa nau omi, ʻo ʻave hono sino ʻo fakatokoto ia ʻi he fonualoto.
And when his disciples heard of it, they came and took up his corpse, and laid it in a tomb.
Pea fakataha ʻae kau ʻaposetolo kia Sisu, ʻonau fakamatala kiate ia ʻae ngaahi meʻa kotoa pē, ʻaia kuo nau fai, mo ia kuo nau ako ʻaki.
And the apostles gathered themselves together unto Jesus, and told him all things, both what they had done, and what they had taught.
Pea pehē ʻe ia kiate kinautolu, “Mou omi ʻakimoutolu pe ki ha potu lala, ʻo mālōlō siʻi:” he naʻe tokolahi naʻe faʻa feʻaluʻaki, pea naʻe ʻikai ke nau ʻataʻatā ke fai ʻenau kai.
And he said unto them, Come ye yourselves apart into a desert place, and rest a while: for there were many coming and going, and they had no leisure so much as to eat.
Pea nau ō fakalilolilo ʻi he vaka ki he potu lala.
And they departed into a desert place by ship privately.
Pea mamata ʻae kakai ki heʻenau ʻalu, pea ʻilo ia ʻe he tokolahi, pea nau feleleʻi ʻuta ki ai mei he kolo kotoa pē, ʻo muʻomuʻa kiate kinautolu, pea fakataha ai kiate ia.
And the people saw them departing, and many knew him, and ran afoot thither out of all cities, and outwent them, and came together unto him.

Pea kuo tuʻu ki ʻuta ʻa Sisu, ʻo ne vakai kuo tokolahi ʻae kakai, naʻe manavaʻofa ia kiate kinautolu, koeʻuhi kuo nau tatau mo e fanga sipi taʻehatauhi: pea ne kamata ako kiate kinautolu ʻae ngaahi meʻa lahi.
And Jesus, when he came out, saw much people, and was moved with compassion toward them, because they were as sheep not having a shepherd: and he began to teach them many things.
Pea kuo tei ʻosi ʻae ʻaho, pea haʻu ʻene kau ākonga kiate ia, ʻo pehē, “Ko e potu lala eni, pea kuo teitei ʻosi ʻae ʻaho:
And when the day was now far spent, his disciples came unto him, and said, This is a desert place, and now the time is far passed:
fekau ke nau ō, koeʻuhi ke nau ʻalu ki he tukuʻuta, mo e ngaahi potu kakai ʻoku tuʻu takatakai, ke nau fakatau maʻanautolu ʻae mā: he ʻoku ʻikai haʻanau meʻa ke kai.”
Send them away, that they may go into the country round about, and into the villages, and buy themselves bread: for they have nothing to eat.
Pea lea ʻe ia, ʻo pehē kiate kinautolu, “Mou ʻatu ha meʻa ke nau kai.” Pea nau pehē kiate ia, Te mau ō, ʻo fakatau mā ʻaki ʻae tenali ʻe uangeau, mo ʻatu ke nau kai?”
He answered and said unto them, Give ye them to eat. And they say unto him, Shall we go and buy two hundred pennyworth of bread, and give them to eat?
Pea pehē ʻe ia kiate kinautolu, “Ko e foʻi mā ʻe fiha ʻoku ʻiate kimoutolu? ʻAlu ʻo vakai.” Pea kuo nau ʻilo, pea nau pehē, “ʻOku nima, mo e ika ʻe ua.”
He saith unto them, How many loaves have ye? go and see. And when they knew, they say, Five, and two fishes.
Pea ne fekau kiate kinautolu ke nau pule ke nofo kotoa pē ki lalo ki he mohuku maʻuiʻui, ʻo tautau tokolahi.
And he commanded them to make all sit down by companies upon the green grass.
Pea naʻa nau nofo ki lalo ʻo fakaʻotu, ʻo tautau toko teau, mo tautau toko nimangofulu.
And they sat down in ranks, by hundreds, and by fifties.

Pea kuo toʻo ʻe ia ʻae foʻi mā ʻe nima mo e ika ʻe ua, pea hanga hake ia ki he langi, ʻo ne tāpuaki, mo ne tofitofi ʻae ngaahi foʻi mā, ʻo ʻange ki heʻene kau ākonga ke tufaki kiate kinautolu; pea ne tufaki mo e ika ʻe ua kiate kinautolu kātoa pe.

And when he had taken the five loaves and the two fishes, he looked up to heaven, and blessed, and brake the loaves, and gave them to his disciples to set before them; and the two fishes divided he among them all.
Pea naʻa nau kai kotoa pē, ʻo mākona.
And they did all eat, and were filled.
Pea nau ʻave ʻae kato ʻe hongofulu ma ua kuo pito ʻi he toenga kai, mo e ika.
And they took up twelve baskets full of the fragments, and of the fishes.
Pea ko kinautolu naʻe kai ʻi he ngaahi foʻi mā, ko e tangata ʻe toko nima afe nai.
And they that did eat of the loaves were about five thousand men.
Pea pule leva ʻe ia ke heka ki vaka ʻa ʻene kau ākonga, ʻo muʻomuʻa ki he potu ʻe taha ki Petesaita, kae fekau ʻe ia ke ʻalu ʻae kakai.
And straightway he constrained his disciples to get into the ship, and to go to the other side before unto Bethsaida, while he sent away the people.
Pea kuo fekau atu ʻakinautolu, naʻe ʻalu ia ki he moʻunga ke lotu ai.
And when he had sent them away, he departed into a mountain to pray.
Pea kuo hoko ʻae efiafi, kuo ʻi he vaha ʻae vaka, kae ʻi ʻuta tokotaha pe ia.
And when even was come, the ship was in the midst of the sea, and he alone on the land.

Pea mamata ia ʻoku nau ongosia ʻi he tau ʻaʻalo; he naʻe tokai ʻae matangi kiate kinautolu: pea kuo ofi hono fā ʻoe leʻo ʻoe pō, pea ʻalu ange ia kiate kinautolu, ʻo ne hāʻele ia ʻi he fukahi tahi, pea hangē ka mole pe ia ʻiate kinautolu.
And he saw them toiling in rowing; for the wind was contrary unto them: and about the fourth watch of the night he cometh unto them, walking upon the sea, and would have passed by them.
Ka ʻi heʻenau mamata ʻoku hāʻele ia ʻi he fukahi vai, naʻa nau mahalo ko e laumālie ia, ʻonau kalanga ai:
But when they saw him walking upon the sea, they supposed it had been a spirit, and cried out:
He naʻa nau mamata kotoa pē kiate ia, pea nau ilifia. Pea leaange leva ia kiate kinautolu, ʻo ne pehē, “Mou fiemālie: he ko au; pea ʻoua ʻe manavahē.”
For they all saw him, and were troubled. And immediately he talked with them, and saith unto them, Be of good cheer: it is I; be not afraid.
Pea ʻalu hake ia kiate kinautolu ki vaka; pea malu leva ʻae matangi: pea fakatumutumu lahi fakamanavahē ʻakinautolu ʻo taʻefaʻalaua ʻi honau loto, mo ofo ai.
And he went up unto them into the ship; and the wind ceased: and they were sore amazed in themselves beyond measure, and wondered.
He naʻe ʻikai te nau manatu ki he ngaahi foʻi mā: he kuo fefeka honau loto.
For they considered not the miracle of the loaves: for their heart was hardened.
Pea kuo nau hoko atu, ʻonau aʻu ki he fonua ko Kenesaleti, pea tau ki ʻuta.
And when they had passed over, they came into the land of Gennesaret, and drew to the shore.
Pea kuo nau haʻu mei he vaka, pea ʻilo leva ia ʻekinautolu.
And when they were come out of the ship, straightway they knew him,
Pea nau feleleʻi ʻi he potu fonua kotoa ko ia mo nau fata fano pe ʻi he ngaahi mohenga ʻakinautolu naʻe mahaki, ki he potu naʻa nau fanongo ʻoku ʻi ai ia.
And ran through that whole region round about, and began to carry about in beds those that were sick, where they heard he was.

Pea naʻe ʻilonga haʻa ne ʻalu ki he ngaahi potu kakai, pe ki he ngaahi kolo, pe ki he tukuʻuta, naʻa nau fakatokoto ʻae mahaki ʻi he ngaahi hala, pea nau kole kiate ia ke nau ala ki he kapa pe ʻo hono kofu: pea ʻilonga ʻakinautolu kotoa pē naʻe ala ki ai, naʻe fakamoʻui ʻakinautolu.

And whithersoever he entered, into villages, or cities, or country, they laid the sick in the streets, and besought him that they might touch if it were but the border of his garment: and as many as touched him were made whole.
Pea toki fakataha kiate ia ʻae kau Fālesi mo e niʻihi ʻi he kau tangata tohi, naʻe haʻu mei Selūsalema.
Then came together unto him the Pharisees, and certain of the scribes, which came from Jerusalem.
Pea ʻi heʻenau mamata ki he niʻihi ʻi heʻene kau ākonga ʻoku nau kai mā ʻi he nima ʻuli, ko e pehē, ko e nima taʻefanofano, naʻa nau hanu ai.
And when they saw some of his disciples eat bread with defiled, that is to say, with unwashen, hands, they found fault.
He ko e kau Fālesi, mo e kakai Siu fulipē, ʻoku ʻikai te nau kai, ʻo kapau ʻe ʻikai te nau fuofua fanofano nima, ko e tokanga ki he talatupuʻa ʻae mātuʻa.
For the Pharisees, and all the Jews, except they wash their hands oft, eat not, holding the tradition of the elders.

Pea ʻi heʻenau haʻu mei he faianga fakatau, ʻoku ʻikai te nau kai, ʻo kapau ʻe ʻikai te nau kaukau. Pea ʻoku ai mo e ngaahi meʻa kehekehe, kuo nau maʻu ke fai, ko e fufulu ʻoe ngaahi ipu inu, mo e ngaahi ipu fua, mo e ngaahi ipu kapa, mo e ngaahi tokotoʻanga.
And when they come from the market, except they wash, they eat not. And many other things there be, which they have received to hold, as the washing of cups, and pots, brasen vessels, and of tables.
Pea fehuʻi kiate ia ʻe he kau Fālesi mo e kau tangata tohi, “Ko e hā ʻoku ʻikai ai ke fai ʻe hoʻo kau ākonga ʻo hangē ko e talatupuʻa ʻae mātuʻa, ka ʻoku nau kai mā mo e nima taʻefanofano?”
Then the Pharisees and scribes asked him, Why walk not thy disciples according to the tradition of the elders, but eat bread with unwashen hands?

Pea leaange ʻe ia, ʻo pehē kiate kinautolu, “Neʻineʻi fakahā ʻe ʻIsaia kiate kimoutolu, ko e kau mālualoi, ʻo hangē ko ia kuo tohi, ‘ʻOku fakaʻapaʻapa ʻae kakai ni kiate au ʻaki honau loungutu, ka ʻoku mamaʻo honau loto ʻiate au.
He answered and said unto them, Well hath Esaias prophesied of you hypocrites, as it is written, This people honoureth me with their lips, but their heart is far from me.
Ka ʻoku taʻeʻaonga ʻenau hū kiate au, he ko e ngaahi akonaki ʻoku nau ako ʻaki, ko e ngaahi fekau ʻae tangata.’
Howbeit in vain do they worship me, teaching for doctrines the commandments of men.
“He kuo mou siʻaki ʻae fekau ʻae ʻOtua, kae maʻu ʻae talatupuʻa ʻae tangata, ko e fufulu ʻoe ngaahi ipu fua mo e ngaahi ipu inu: pea ʻoku lahi mo e ngaahi meʻa pehē ʻoku mou fai.
For laying aside the commandment of God, ye hold the tradition of men, as the washing of pots and cups: and many other such like things ye do.
Pea pehē ʻe ia kiate kinautolu, “Ha meʻa ʻe lelei ko hoʻomou liʻaki ʻae fekau ʻae ʻOtua, ka mou fai ʻae talatupuʻa ʻamoutolu.
And he said unto them, Full well ye reject the commandment of God, that ye may keep your own tradition.
He naʻe pehē ʻe Mōsese, ‘Fakaʻapaʻapa ki hoʻo tamai mo hoʻo faʻē;’ pea, ‘Ko ia ʻoku kape ki heʻene tamai pe ko ʻene faʻē, tuku ke mate tāmateʻi ia.’
For Moses said, Honour thy father and thy mother; and, Whoso curseth father or mother, let him die the death:
Ka ʻoku mou pehē, ‘Kapau ʻe lea ha tangata ki heʻene tamai pe ko ʻene faʻē, ʻo pehē, “Ko ʻeku meʻa kotoa pē ʻoku ʻaonga kiate koe, ko e Kopano ia,”’ ʻaia ko e foaki tapu; ʻe ʻataʻatā ia.
But ye say, If a man shall say to his father or mother, It is Corban, that is to say, a gift, by whatsoever thou mightest be profited by me; he shall be free.
Pea ʻoku mou taʻofi haʻane toe fai ha meʻa maʻa ʻene tamai pe ko ʻene faʻē;
And ye suffer him no more to do ought for his father or his mother;
‌ʻO fakataʻeʻaonga ʻae folofola ʻae ʻOtua ʻaki hoʻomou talatupuʻa, ʻaia ʻoku mou enginakiʻaki: pea ʻoku lahi ʻae meʻa pehē ʻoku mou fai.”
Making the word of God of none effect through your tradition, which ye have delivered: and many such like things do ye.
Pea ʻi heʻene ui mai ʻae kakai kotoa pē, naʻa ne pehē kiate kinautolu, “Fanongo kotoa pē kiate au, pea ʻilo.
And when he had called all the people unto him, he said unto them, Hearken unto me every one of you, and understand:
‌ʻOku ʻikai ha meʻa ʻituʻa ʻi he tangata, pea hū ki ai, te ne faʻa fakaʻuliʻi ia: ka ko e ngaahi meʻa ʻoku haʻu meiate ia, ko ia ia ʻoku fakaʻuliʻi ʻae tangata.
There is nothing from without a man, that entering into him can defile him: but the things which come out of him, those are they that defile the man.
Ko e tangata ʻoku telinga ke ongo, ke ongoʻi ia.”
If any man have ears to hear, let him hear.
Pea kuo hū ia ki he fale mei he kakai, naʻe fehuʻi ʻe heʻene kau ākonga kiate ia ki he fakatātā.
And when he was entered into the house from the people, his disciples asked him concerning the parable.
Pea pehē ʻe ia kiate kinautolu, “He ʻoku pehē hoʻomou taʻeʻilo foki? ʻOku ʻikai te mou ʻilo, ko e meʻa kotoa pē mei tuʻa, ʻoku ʻalu ki he tangata, ʻoku ʻikai faʻa fakaʻuli ia ʻe ia;
And he saith unto them, Are ye so without understanding also? Do ye not perceive, that whatsoever thing from without entereth into the man, it cannot defile him;
Koeʻuhi ʻoku ʻikai ke ʻalu ia ki hono loto, ka ki he kete, ʻoku fakamaʻa ai ʻae meʻakai kotoa pē, kae toki ʻalu kituʻa ʻae meʻa taʻeʻaonga?”
Because it entereth not into his heart, but into the belly, and goeth out into the draught, purging all meats?
Pea pehē ʻe ia, “Ko ia ʻoku haʻu mei he tangata, ko ia ia ʻoku fakaʻuliʻi ʻae tangata.
And he said, That which cometh out of the man, that defileth the man.
He ʻoku mei loto, mei he loto ʻoe tangata, ʻae mahalo kovi, mo e tonoʻi fefine mo e feʻauaki, mo e fakapō,
For from within, out of the heart of men, proceed evil thoughts, adulteries, fornications, murders,
Mo e kaihaʻa, mo e manumanu, mo e angahala, mo e kākā, mo e anga fakalielia, mo e mata kovi, mo e lea kovi, mo e laukau, mo e vale:
Thefts, covetousness, wickedness, deceit, lasciviousness, an evil eye, blasphemy, pride, foolishness:
Ko e ngaahi meʻa kovi ni kotoa pē ʻoku haʻu mei he loto, ʻoku fakaʻuliʻi ʻae tangata.”
All these evil things come from within, and defile the man.
Pea tuʻu hake ia ʻi ai, ʻo ʻalu ki he potu ʻo Taia mo Saitoni, pea ne hū ki he fale, ʻo ne loto ke ʻoua naʻa ʻilo ia ʻe ha taha: ka naʻe ʻikai faʻa fakapuli ia.
And from thence he arose, and went into the borders of Tyre and Sidon, and entered into an house, and would have no man know it: but he could not be hid.
He naʻe ongoa atu ia ki ha fefine naʻe ai ʻene taʻahine siʻi naʻe ʻi ai ʻae laumālie ʻuli, pea haʻu ia, ʻo tōmapeʻe ʻi hono vaʻe:
For a certain woman, whose young daughter had an unclean spirit, heard of him, and came and fell at his feet:
Ko e Kiliki ʻae fefine ni, mei he puleʻanga ko Sailofinisia: pea naʻa ne kole kiate ia, ke ne kapusi kituʻa ʻae tēvolo ʻi heʻene taʻahine.
The woman was a Greek, a Syrophenician by nation; and she besought him that he would cast forth the devil out of her daughter.
Ka naʻe pehē ʻe Sisu kiate ia, “ʻOua ke tomuʻa mākona ʻae fānau: he ʻoku ʻikai ngali ke toʻo ʻae mā ʻae fānau, mo lī ki he fanga kulī.”
But Jesus said unto her, Let the children first be filled: for it is not meet to take the children’s bread, and to cast it unto the dogs.
Pea leaange ʻe ia, ʻo pehē kiate ia, “Ko e moʻoni, ʻEiki: ka ʻoku kai ʻe he fanga kulī, ʻi he lalo keinangaʻanga, ʻae momo ʻoe meʻakai ʻae fānau.”
And she answered and said unto him, Yes, Lord: yet the dogs under the table eat of the children’s crumbs.
Pea pehē ʻe ia kiate ia, “Koeʻuhi ko e lea ni ke ke ʻalu; kuo ʻalu kituʻa ʻae tēvolo ʻi hoʻo taʻahine.”
And he said unto her, For this saying go thy way; the devil is gone out of thy daughter.
Pea kuo hoko ia ki hono fale, pea ne ʻilo kuo ʻalu kituʻa ʻa e tēvolo, kae tokoto ʻene taʻahine ʻi he mohenga.
And when she was come to her house, she found the devil gone out, and her daughter laid upon the bed.
Pea naʻe toe ʻalu ia mei he potu ʻo Taia mo Saitoni, ʻo haʻu ʻi he potu fonua ʻo Tikapolisi, ki he tahi ʻo Kāleli.
And again, departing from the coasts of Tyre and Sidon, he came unto the sea of Galilee, through the midst of the coasts of Decapolis.
Pea nau ʻomi kiate ia ha tokotaha naʻe tuli, pea ʻikai ke faʻa lea; pea naʻa nau kole kiate ia ke ne hilifaki hono nima ki ai.
And they bring unto him one that was deaf, and had an impediment in his speech; and they beseech him to put his hand upon him.
Pea naʻa ne fakaafe ia mei he kakai, ʻo ne ʻai hono tuhu ki hono telinga, pea ʻaʻanu, mo ne ala ki hono ʻelelo;
And he took him aside from the multitude, and put his fingers into his ears, and he spit, and touched his tongue;
Pea hanga hake ia ki he langi, ʻo mafulu, mo ne pehē kiate ia, “ʻEfata,” ko e pehē ia, “Ke ava.”
And looking up to heaven, he sighed, and saith unto him, Ephphatha, that is, Be opened.
Pea naʻe ava leva hono telinga, pea vete ʻae noʻo ʻo hono ʻelelo, pea ne lea totonu.
And straightway his ears were opened, and the string of his tongue was loosed, and he spake plain.
Pea ne fekau kiate kinautolu ke ʻoua naʻa nau fakahā ki ha taha: ka ʻi heʻene fekau lahi kiate kinautolu, ne ʻāsili ai ʻo lahi ʻenau fanongonongo ia;
And he charged them that they should tell no man: but the more he charged them, so much the more a great deal they published it;
Pea naʻa nau ofo ʻo lahi ʻaupito, ʻo pehē, “Kuo ne fai ʻae ngaahi meʻa kotoa pē ʻo lelei: ʻoku ne ngaohi ʻae tuli ke ongo, mo e noa ke lea.”
And were beyond measure astonished, saying, He hath done all things well: he maketh both the deaf to hear, and the dumb to speak.
‌ʻI he ngaahi ʻaho ko ia naʻe fuʻu tokolahi ʻaupito ʻae kakai, pea naʻe ʻikai haʻanau meʻa ke kai, pea ui ʻe Sisu ʻa ʻene kau ākonga, ʻo ne pehē kiate kinautolu,
In those days the multitude being very great, and having nothing to eat, Jesus called his disciples unto him, and saith unto them,
“ʻOku ou ʻofa mamahi ki he kakai, koeʻuhi ʻoku ʻaho tolu ʻenau ʻiate au, pea ʻoku ʻikai haʻanau meʻa ke kai:
I have compassion on the multitude, because they have now been with me three days, and have nothing to eat:
Pea kapau te u fekau kenau ʻalu fiekaia ki honau ngaahi fale, te nau pongia ʻi he hala: he ko honau niʻihi kuo haʻu mei he mamaʻo.”
And if I send them away fasting to their own houses, they will faint by the way: for divers of them came from far.
Pea pehēange ʻene kau ākonga kiate ia, “ʻE maʻu mei fē ʻe ha taha ʻae mā ke fakamākona ʻaki ʻakinautolu ni ʻi heni ʻi he toafa?”
And his disciples answered him, From whence can a man satisfy these men with bread here in the wilderness?
Pea fehuʻi ia kiate kinautolu, “ʻOku fiha hoʻomou foʻi mā?” Pea nau pehē, “ʻOku fitu.”
And he asked them, How many loaves have ye? And they said, Seven.

Pea fekau ʻe ia ki he kakai ke nau nofo ki lalo ki he kelekele; pea ne toʻo ʻae foʻi mā ʻe fitu, ʻo ne fakafetaʻi, mo tofitofi, pea ʻange ki heʻene kau ākonga ke tufaki; pea naʻa nau tufaki ia ʻi he ʻao ʻoe kakai.
And he commanded the people to sit down on the ground: and he took the seven loaves, and gave thanks, and brake, and gave to his disciples to set before them; and they did set them before the people.
Pea naʻa nau maʻu mo e ngaahi ika iiki: pea ne ne tāpuaki, mo fekau ke tufaki foki ia.
And they had a few small fishes: and he blessed, and commanded to set them also before them.
Pea naʻa nau kai, ʻo mākona: pea nau tānaki ʻae toenga kai ko e kato ʻe fitu.
So they did eat, and were filled: and they took up of the broken meat that was left seven baskets.
Pea ko kinautolu naʻe kai, ko e toko fā afe nai: pea naʻe fekau ʻe ia ke nau ʻalu.
And they that had eaten were about four thousand: and he sent them away.
Pea heka vaka leva ia mo ʻene kau ākonga, ʻo haʻu ki he potu ʻo Talamanutā.
And straightway he entered into a ship with his disciples, and came into the parts of Dalmanutha.
Pea ʻalu ange ʻae kau Fālesi, ʻo kamata fakafehuʻi kiate ia, mo kumi ʻiate ia ha fakaʻilonga mei he langi, ko hono ʻahiʻahiʻi.
And the Pharisees came forth, and began to question with him, seeking of him a sign from heaven, tempting him.

Pea mafulu lahi ia ʻi hono laumālie, mo pehē, “Ko e hā ʻoku kumi ai ʻe he toʻutangata ni ha fakaʻilonga? Ko e moʻoni ʻoku ou tala atu kiate kimoutolu, ʻE ʻikai tuku ha fakaʻilonga ki he toʻutangata ni.”
And he sighed deeply in his spirit, and saith, Why doth this generation seek after a sign? verily I say unto you, There shall no sign be given unto this generation.
Pea ʻalu ia ʻiate kinautolu, ʻo toe heka vaka, mo ʻalu ki he kauvai ʻe taha.
And he left them, and entering into the ship again departed to the other side.
Pea kuo ngaloʻi he kau ākonga ke ʻave ha mā, pea ko e foʻi mā pe taha naʻe ʻi he vaka mo kinautolu.
Now the disciples had forgotten to take bread, neither had they in the ship with them more than one loaf.
Pea naʻa ne naʻinaʻi kiate kinautolu, ʻo pehē, “Tokanga, pea vakai telia ʻae meʻa fakatupu ʻae kau Fālesi, pea mo e meʻa fakatupu ʻa Helota.”
And he charged them, saying, Take heed, beware of the leaven of the Pharisees, and of the leaven of Herod.
Pea fealēleaʻaki ai ʻakinautolu, ʻo pehē, “Ko e meʻa ʻi heʻetau taʻeʻomi ha mā.”
And they reasoned among themselves, saying, It is because we have no bread.
Pea kuo ʻilo ia ʻe Sisu, pea pehē ʻe ia kiate kinautolu, “Ko e hā ʻoku mou alea ai, ʻi he ʻikai haʻamou mā? ʻOku teʻeki ai te mou mamata, pe ʻilo? ʻOku kei fefeka homou loto?
And when Jesus knew it, he saith unto them, Why reason ye, because ye have no bread? perceive ye not yet, neither understand? have ye your heart yet hardened?
‌ʻOku mou mata, kae ʻikai te mou mamata? Pea telinga, kae ʻikai ongoʻi? Pea ʻoku ʻikai te mou manatu?
Having eyes, see ye not? and having ears, hear ye not? and do ye not remember?
‌ʻI heʻeku tofitofi ʻae foʻi mā ʻe nima ki he toko nima afe, naʻe fiha ʻae kato naʻe pito ʻi he toenga ne mou ʻave?” Pea nau pehē kiate ia, “E hongofulu ma ua.”
When I brake the five loaves among five thousand, how many baskets full of fragments took ye up? They say unto him, Twelve.
“Pea ko e fitu ki he toko fā afe, naʻe fiha ʻae kato naʻe pito ʻi he toenga ne mou ʻave?” Pea nau pehē, “ʻE fitu.”
And when the seven among four thousand, how many baskets full of fragments took ye up? And they said, Seven.
Pea pehē ʻe ia kiate kinautolu, “Ko e hā nai ʻoku ʻikai ai te mou ʻilo?”
And he said unto them, How is it that ye do not understand?
Pea haʻu ia ki Petesaita: pea naʻa nau ʻomi kiate ia ʻae tangata kui, ʻonau kole kiate ia ke ne ala ki ai.
And he cometh to Bethsaida; and they bring a blind man unto him, and besought him to touch him.
Pea puke ʻe ia ʻae nima ʻoe tangata kui, ʻo tataki ia kituʻa mei he potu kakai; pea kuo ne ʻaʻanu ki hono mata, mo ʻai hono nima kiate ia, pea ne fehuʻi kiate ia, pe ʻoku ne mamata ki ha meʻa.
And he took the blind man by the hand, and led him out of the town; and when he had spit on his eyes, and put his hands upon him, he asked him if he saw ought.
Pea hanga hake ia, ʻo ne pehē, “ʻOku ou mamata ki he kakai ʻoku hangē ko e ngaahi ʻakau, ʻoku ʻeveʻeva.”
And he looked up, and said, I see men as trees, walking.
Pea hili ia, pea ne toe ʻai hono nima ki hono mata, pea fekau kiate ia ke ne hanga hake: pea naʻe moʻui ia, ʻo ne mamata totonu ki he kakai kotoa pē.
After that he put his hands again upon his eyes, and made him look up: and he was restored, and saw every man clearly.
Pea ne fekau ia ki hono fale, mo ne pehē, “ʻOua naʻa ke ʻalu ki he potu kakai, pe tala ia ki ha taha ʻi he potu kakai.”
And he sent him away to his house, saying, Neither go into the town, nor tell it to any in the town.

Pea ʻalu atu ʻa Sisu, mo ʻene kau ākonga, ki he ngaahi potu kakai ʻo Sesalia ʻi Filipai: pea fehuʻi ʻe ia ki heʻene kau ākonga ʻi he hala, ʻo ne pehē kiate kinautolu, “ʻOku pehē ʻe he kakai pe ko hai au?”
And Jesus went out, and his disciples, into the towns of Caesarea Philippi: and by the way he asked his disciples, saying unto them, Whom do men say that I am?
Pea nau pehēange, “Ko Sione ko e Papitaiso: kaepehē ʻe he niʻihi, ko ʻIlaisiā; pea pehē ʻe he niʻihi, ko e taha ʻoe kau palōfita.”
And they answered, John the Baptist: but some say, Elias; and others, One of the prophets.
Pea pehē ʻe ia kiate kinautolu, “Ka ʻoku pehē ʻekimoutolu ko hai au?” Pea lea ʻa Pita, ʻo pehēange kiate ia, “Ko koe, ko e Kalaisi.”
And he saith unto them, But whom say ye that I am? And Peter answereth and saith unto him, Thou art the Christ.
Pea fekau ʻe ia kiate kinautolu ke ʻoua naʻa nau fakahā ia ki ha taha.
And he charged them that they should tell no man of him.

Pea kamata fakahā ʻe ia kiate kinautolu, “ʻAe kātaki ʻe he Foha ʻoe tangata ʻae ngaahi meʻa lahi, pea siʻaki ia ʻe he mātuʻa, mo e kau taulaʻeiki lahi, mo e kau tangata tohi, pea ʻe tāmateʻi ia, pea hili ʻae ʻaho ʻe tolu ʻe toe tuʻu.”
And he began to teach them, that the Son of man must suffer many things, and be rejected of the elders, and of the chief priests, and scribes, and be killed, and after three days rise again.
Pea naʻa ne lea ʻilongofua ʻaki ʻae lea ko ia. Pea ʻave ia ʻe Pita, ʻo ne kamata valokiʻi ia.
And he spake that saying openly. And Peter took him, and began to rebuke him.

Ka kuo tafoki ia ki mui, ʻo vakai ki heʻene kau ākonga, pea valokiʻi ʻe ia ʻa Pita, ʻo pehē, “ʻAlu ki hoku tuʻa, Sētane: he ʻoku ʻikai te ke leleiʻia ʻi he ngaahi meʻa ʻae ʻOtua, ka ʻi he ngaahi meʻa ʻae tangata.”
But when he had turned about and looked on his disciples, he rebuked Peter, saying, Get thee behind me, Satan: for thou savourest not the things that be of God, but the things that be of men.
Pea kuo ui ʻe ia ʻae kakai mo ʻene kau ākonga foki, pea ne pehē kiate kinautolu, “Ko ia ia ʻoku loto ke muimui ʻiate au, ke ne siʻaki ʻe ia ia, kae toʻo ʻene kavenga, ʻo muimui ʻiate au.
And when he had called the people unto him with his disciples also, he said unto them, Whosoever will come after me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross, and follow me.
He ko ia ia ʻoku loto ke kalofaki ʻene moʻui, ʻe mole ia: ka ko ia ia ʻe mole ʻene moʻui koeʻuhi ko au mo e ongoongolelei, ʻe maʻu ʻe ia ia.
For whosoever will save his life shall lose it; but whosoever shall lose his life for my sake and the gospel’s, the same shall save it.
He ko e hā hono ʻaonga ki ha tangata, ʻo kapau ʻe maʻu ʻe ia ʻa māmani kotoa pē, kae mole hono laumālie ʻoʻona?
For what shall it profit a man, if he shall gain the whole world, and lose his own soul?
Pe ko e hā ʻe foaki ʻe ha tangata ke fetongi ʻaki hono laumālie?
Or what shall a man give in exchange for his soul?

Ko ia ia ʻe mā kiate au, mo ʻeku ngaahi lea, ʻi he toʻutangata feʻauaki mo angahala ni, ʻe ma foki ʻae Foha ʻoe tangata ʻiate ia, ʻoka haʻu ia ʻi he nāunau ʻo ʻene Tamai, mo e kau ʻāngelo māʻoniʻoni.”

Whosoever therefore shall be ashamed of me and of my words in this adulterous and sinful generation; of him also shall the Son of man be ashamed, when he cometh in the glory of his Father with the holy angels.

Pea pehē ʻe ia kiate kinautolu, “Ko e moʻoni ʻoku ou tala atu kiate kimoutolu, ʻOku ai ʻae niʻihi ʻiate kinautolu ʻoku tutuʻu ʻi heni, ʻe ʻikai te nau kamata ʻae mate, kaeʻoua ke nau mamata ki he puleʻanga ʻoe ʻOtua ʻoku hoko mai mo e mālohi.”
And he said unto them, Verily I say unto you, That there be some of them that stand here, which shall not taste of death, till they have seen the kingdom of God come with power.
