And the scripture was fulfilled, which saith, And he was numbered with the transgressors.
Pea manukiʻi ia ʻekinautolu naʻe feʻaluʻaki, ʻi he kalokalo honau ʻulu, mo e pehē, “ʻA koe, ʻoku ke maumauʻi ʻae falelotu lahi, mo toe langa ia ʻi he ʻaho ʻe tolu,
And they that passed by railed on him, wagging their heads, and saying, Ah, thou that destroyest the temple, and buildest it in three days,
Fakamoʻui koe, pea ke ʻalu hifo mei he ʻakau.”
Save thyself, and come down from the cross.
Pea manuki pehē foki ʻe he kau taulaʻeiki lahi, ʻo nau fepehēʻaki ʻiate kinautolu mo e kau tangata tohi, “Naʻa ne fakamoʻui ʻae kakai; ka ʻoku ʻikai te ne faʻa fakamoʻui ia.
Likewise also the chief priests mocking said among themselves with the scribes, He saved others; himself he cannot save.
Tuku ke ʻalu hifo eni ʻa Kalaisi ko e Tuʻi ʻo ʻIsileli mei he ʻakau, koeʻuhi ke mau mamata mo tui.” Pea ko kinaua naʻe tutuki ki he ʻakau mo ia ne na manukiʻi ia.
Let Christ the King of Israel descend now from the cross, that we may see and believe. And they that were crucified with him reviled him.
Pea ʻi he hokosia hono ono ʻoe feituʻulaʻā, naʻe fakapoʻuli ʻae fonua kotoa ʻo aʻu ki hono hiva ʻoe feituʻulaʻā.
And when the sixth hour was come, there was darkness over the whole land until the ninth hour.
Pea ʻi hono hiva ʻoe feituʻulaʻā naʻe tangi leʻo lahi ʻa Sisu, ʻo pehē, “ʻIlai, ʻIlai, lama sapakatani?” ʻAia ko hono ʻuhinga, “Ko hoku ʻOtua, ko hoku ʻOtua, ko e hā kuo ke liʻaki ai au?”
And at the ninth hour Jesus cried with a loud voice, saying, Eloi, Eloi, lama sabachthani? which is, being interpreted, My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?
Pea ko honau niʻihi naʻe tutuʻu ʻi ai, ʻi heʻenau fanongo, naʻa nau pehē, “Vakai, ʻoku ne ui kia ʻIlaisiā.”
And some of them that stood by, when they heard it, said, Behold, he calleth Elias.
Pea lele ʻae tokotaha, ʻo ne unu ʻae oma ki he vai mahi, ʻo ʻai ia ki he vaʻa kaho, mo ʻohake ke ne inu, mo ne pehē, “Tuku ai pe; ke tau vakai, pe haʻu ʻa ʻIlaisiā ke tuku hifo ia.”
And one ran and filled a spunge full of vinegar, and put it on a reed, and gave him to drink, saying, Let alone; let us see whether Elias will come to take him down.
Pea tangi leʻo lahi ʻa Sisu, pea ne tuku hake hono laumālie.
And Jesus cried with a loud voice, and gave up the ghost.
Pea naʻe mahae ua ʻae puipui ʻoe falelotu lahi, mei hono potu ʻi ʻolunga ʻo aʻu ki lalo.
And the veil of the temple was rent in twain from the top to the bottom.
Pea ʻi he mamata ʻae ʻeikitau, naʻe tuʻu ʻo hangatonu atu kiate ia, kuo pehē ʻa ʻene tangi, mo e tuku hake ʻa hono laumālie, ne ne pehē, “Tā ko e moʻoni ko e ʻAlo ʻoe ʻOtua ʻae tangata ni.”
And when the centurion, which stood over against him, saw that he so cried out, and gave up the ghost, he said, Truly this man was the Son of God.
Naʻe ai mo e kau fefine naʻa nau sio mai mei he mamaʻo: pea naʻe ʻiate kinautolu ʻa Mele Makitaline, mo Mele ko e faʻē ʻa Semisi siʻi pea mo Sose, mo Salome;
There were also women looking on afar off: among whom was Mary Magdalene, and Mary the mother of James the less and of Joses, and Salome;
(ʻAkinautolu foki naʻa nau muimui kiate ia, mo tauhi ia ʻi heʻene ʻi Kāleli;) pea mo e kau fefine tokolahi, naʻa nau ʻalu hake mo ia ki Selūsalema.
(Who also, when he was in Galilee, followed him, and ministered unto him;) and many other women which came up with him unto Jerusalem.
Pea kuo efiafi ai, pea koeʻuhi ko e teuteu, ʻaia ko e ʻaho ʻoku muʻa ʻi he ʻaho Sāpate,
And now when the even was come, because it was the preparation, that is, the day before the sabbath,
Naʻe ʻalu loto mālohi ʻa Siosefa ʻo ʻAlematea, ko e fakamaau ongolelei, pea naʻe tatali foki ia ki he puleʻanga ʻoe ʻOtua, ʻo ne kole meia Pailato ʻae sino ʻo Sisu.
Joseph of Arimathaea, an honourable counsellor, which also waited for the kingdom of God, came, and went in boldly unto Pilate, and craved the body of Jesus.
Pea ofo ʻa Pailato ʻi heʻene pekia vave: pea ne ui ʻae ʻeikitau, ʻo fehuʻi ki ai pe kuo fuoloa ange ʻene pekia.
And Pilate marvelled if he were already dead: and calling unto him the centurion, he asked him whether he had been any while dead.
Pea kuo ne ʻiloia mei he ʻeikitau, pea ne ʻatu ʻae sino kia Siosefa.
And when he knew it of the centurion, he gave the body to Joseph.

Pea fakatau ʻe ia ʻae tupenu mahuʻinga lelei, mo vete hifo ia, ʻo fakakoloaʻaki ia ʻae tupenu mahuʻinga, pea fakatokoto ia ʻi he fonualoto kuo tā ʻi he maka, pea ne teketekaʻi ʻae maka ki he matapā ʻoe fonualoto.
And he bought fine linen, and took him down, and wrapped him in the linen, and laid him in a sepulchre which was hewn out of a rock, and rolled a stone unto the door of the sepulchre.
Pea ko Mele Makitaline mo Meleko e faʻē ʻa Sose, ne na mamata ki he potu kuo fakatokoto aiia.
And Mary Magdalene and Mary the mother of Joses beheld where he was laid.
Pea ʻi he hili ʻae Sāpate, kuo fakatau ʻe Mele Makitaline, mo Mele ko e faʻē ʻa Semisi, mo Salome, ʻae ngaahi ʻakau namu lelei, koeʻuhi ke nau omi ʻo fakatolongaʻaki ia.
And when the sabbath was past, Mary Magdalene, and Mary the mother of James, and Salome, had bought sweet spices, that they might come and anoint him.
Pea ʻi he hengihengi ʻoe ʻuluaki ʻaho ʻoe uike, naʻa nau omi ki he fonualoto, feʻunga mo e ʻalu hake ʻae laʻā.
And very early in the morning the first day of the week, they came unto the sepulchre at the rising of the sun.
Pea naʻa nau fepehēʻaki, “Ko hai te ne teketekaʻi maʻatautolu ʻae maka mei he matapā ʻoe fonualoto?”
And they said among themselves, Who shall roll us away the stone from the door of the sepulchre?
Pea ʻi heʻenau sio, naʻa nau ʻilo kuo tekaʻi atu ʻae maka: he naʻe lahi ʻaupito ia.
And when they looked, they saw that the stone was rolled away: for it was very great.
Pea ʻi he hū ki he fonualoto, naʻa nau mamata ki ha talavou ʻoku nofo ʻi he potu toʻomataʻu, kuo kofuʻaki ʻae kofu tōtōlofa mo hinehina; pea naʻa nau ilifia.
And entering into the sepulchre, they saw a young man sitting on the right side, clothed in a long white garment; and they were affrighted.

Pea pehē ʻe ia kiate kinautolu, “ʻOua te mou ilifia: ʻOku mou kumi ʻa Sisu ʻo Nāsaleti, ʻaia naʻe tutuki ki he ʻakau: kuo tuʻu hake ia; ʻoku ʻikai ʻi heni ia; vakai ki he potu naʻa nau fakatokoto ai ia.
And he saith unto them, Be not affrighted: Ye seek Jesus of Nazareth, which was crucified: he is risen; he is not here: behold the place where they laid him.
Ka mou ō, ʻo fakahā ki heʻene kau ākonga mo Pita, ʻoku muʻomuʻa ia ʻiate kimoutolu ki Kāleli: te mou mamata kiate ia ʻi ai, ʻo hangē ko ʻene tala kiate kimoutolu.”
But go your way, tell his disciples and Peter that he goeth before you into Galilee: there shall ye see him, as he said unto you.
Pea naʻa nau hū leva kituʻa, ʻo feholaki mei he fonualoto; he naʻa nau tetetete mo ilifia: pea ʻikai te nau lea siʻi ki ha taha; he naʻa nau manavahē.
And they went out quickly, and fled from the sepulchre; for they trembled and were amazed: neither said they any thing to any man; for they were afraid.
Pea kuo toetuʻu ʻa Sisu ʻi he hengihengi ʻoe ʻuluaki ʻaho ʻoe uike, naʻa ne tomuʻa fakahā ia kia Mele Makitaline, ʻaia ne ne kapusi mei ai ʻae tēvolo ʻe toko fitu.
Now when Jesus was risen early the first day of the week, he appeared first to Mary Magdalene, out of whom he had cast seven devils.
Pea ʻalu ia ʻo fakahā kiate kinautolu naʻa nau ʻiate ia, lolotonga ʻenau mamahi mo tangi.
And she went and told them that had been with him, as they mourned and wept.
Pea ko kinautolu, ʻi heʻenau fanongo kuo moʻui ia, pea kuo mamata ia ki ai, naʻe ʻikai te nau tui.
And they, when they had heard that he was alive, and had been seen of her, believed not.
Pea hili eni ne hā ia ʻi he anga ʻe taha ki honau tokoua, ʻi heʻena ō ʻo fononga ki he potu tukuʻuta.
After that he appeared in another form unto two of them, as they walked, and went into the country.
Pea naʻa na ō, ʻo fakahā ia kiate kinautolu; ka naʻe ʻikai te nau tui kiate kinaua.
And they went and told it unto the residue: neither believed they them.

Pea hili ia, naʻa ne hā ki he toko hongofulu ma tokotaha ʻi heʻenau nofo ʻo kai, ʻo ne valokiʻi ʻenau taʻetui mo loto fefeka, ko e meʻa ʻi heʻenau taʻetui kiate kinautolu naʻa nau mamata kiate ia ʻi he hili ʻene toetuʻu.
Afterward he appeared unto the eleven as they sat at meat, and upbraided them with their unbelief and hardness of heart, because they believed not them which had seen him after he was risen.
Pea pehē ʻe ia kiate kinautolu, “Mou ʻalu ki māmani kotoa pē, ʻo malangaʻaki ʻae ongoongolelei ki he kakai fulipē.
And he said unto them, Go ye into all the world, and preach the gospel to every creature.
Ko ia ia ʻe tui mo papitaiso, ʻe moʻui; ka ko ia ia ʻe ʻikai tui, ʻe malaʻia.
He that believeth and is baptized shall be saved; but he that believeth not shall be damned.
Pea ko e ngaahi fakaʻilonga eni ʻe hoko kiate kinautolu ʻoku tui: Te nau kapusi ʻae kau tēvolo ʻi hoku huafa; te nau lea ʻaki ʻae ngaahi lea foʻou;
And these signs shall follow them that believe; In my name shall they cast out devils; they shall speak with new tongues;
Te nau toʻo hake ʻae ngaahi ngata; pea kapau te nau inu ha meʻa fakamate, ʻe ʻikai kovi ia kiate kinautolu; te nau hilifaki nima ki he mahaki, pea te nau moʻui.”
They shall take up serpents; and if they drink any deadly thing, it shall not hurt them; they shall lay hands on the sick, and they shall recover.
Ko ia hili ʻae lea ʻae ʻEiki kiate kinautolu, naʻe maʻu hake ia ki he langi ʻo nofo ʻi he nima toʻomataʻu ʻoe ʻOtua.
So then after the Lord had spoken unto them, he was received up into heaven, and sat on the right hand of God.
Pea naʻa nau ʻalu atu, ʻo malanga ʻi he potu kotoa pē, pea naʻe ngāue ʻae ʻEiki mo kinautolu, ʻo ne fakamoʻoni ʻae folofola ʻaki ʻae ngaahi fakaʻilonga naʻe hoko. ʻEmeni.
And they went forth, and preached every where, the Lord working with them, and confirming the word with signs following. Amen.
